documentControl.title: Tumor Evaluation Review Agent — Programming Specification

changeHistory.revision: Initial draft: definitions, data contracts, processing pipeline, derivation algorithms, rule catalog (6 families, 61 review points), LLM integration contract, query reconciliation, output specification, API surface, testing and extensibility.

documentControl.reviewInstructions: Reviewers should read first (the arithmetic everything else depends on), then review the rule catalog family by family. For each rule, confirm: (a) the logic matches sponsor practice, (b) the severity is right, (c) the suggested query wording matches house style, (d) the false-positive guards are sufficient. Mark rules to ACCEPT, AMEND or REMOVE. Rules whose <status> is PROPOSED_OPTIONAL are switched off by default and need an explicit decision.

enumeration.value: Complete response
Partial response
Stable disease

Not evaluable

enumeration.value: Complete response
Non-CR / Non-PD

value.note: Only for subjects without measurable disease at baseline

enumeration.name: Severity
enumeration.value: Affects a primary or key secondary endpoint derivation (response, progression, date of progression) or subject eligibility. Must be resolved before database lock.
Affects data integrity or guideline conformance with plausible endpoint impact.
Conformance or consistency issue with no current endpoint impact.
Observation for awareness; low confidence or expected-but-worth-noting pattern.

enumeration.name: DeterminationMode
enumeration.value: Verdict computed entirely by rule logic. Confidence 1.0.
Verdict depends on a model judgement over free text or clinical narrative. Confidence reported and calibrated.
Deterministic trigger; model adds classification or context that may downgrade to INFO.

enumeration.name: QueryLinkStatus
enumeration.value: No prior query covers this finding.
An open query already covers it; finding is suppressed from the default worklist and linked.
A query was answered and the data now passes; finding is not raised (recorded for audit only).
A query was answered or closed but the data still fails; finding is escalated one severity level.
The same dedupe key was raised, resolved, and has re-appeared in a later run.

enumeration.name: RuleStatus
enumeration.value: On by default.
Implemented but off by default; requires sponsor decision at the Step 2 gate.
Activates only when its required fields and configuration are present.

interpretationDecisions.note: Points where the guidelines are silent or ambiguous. Each is configuration with a stated default; all require confirmation at the Step 2 gate.

decision.topic: Reappearance of a target lesion that had resolved
decision.default: The lesion re-enters the sum of diameters at its measured size; it is NOT treated as a new lesion. Progression is then judged by the nadir rule.
decision.alternative: Some protocols treat reappearance of a lesion after CR as progression. If the protocol says so, set reappearance_is_progression=true.

decision.default: Contributes the configured default of 5 mm to the sum, and the lesion is not considered absent (so CR is not assignable).
decision.alternative: Record actual estimated size where the eCRF permits it. The rule set flags inconsistent use of the two conventions within a study.

decision.topic: Nodal target lesions in the sum
decision.default: Nodal target lesions remain in the sum at every timepoint using short axis, even when the short axis falls below 10 mm. The sum therefore need not reach zero for CR.
decision.note: A frequent site error is setting nodal targets to 0 to force CR; rule TE-FU-009 detects it.

decision.topic: Non-evaluable target lesion at a timepoint
decision.default: Target response is NE, unless progression can be established from the measured lesions alone (sum of measured lesions already meets the PD threshold against nadir) or from a new lesion, in which case PD is assignable.

Compute in full precision; compare against thresholds with a tolerance of 1e-6; round only for display to one decimal place. A reported value is considered discrepant only outside a configured tolerance (default 0.5 mm on sums, 0.1 percentage point on percentages).

decision.topic: Baseline for percent change after a change of baseline scan
decision.default: Baseline is the last evaluable assessment on or before first dose within the protocol window; if multiple exist, the one closest to first dose.
Excluded from best-overall-response derivation; retained in the data and still checked for internal consistency.

decision.topic: Unequivocal non-target progression in the presence of measurable disease
decision.default: Raised for review whenever non-target PD is recorded while target response is CR/PR/SD and no new lesion exists, because the guideline treats this as an exceptional circumstance requiring substantial overall worsening.

ingestionRules.rule: Units normalised to millimetres; original value and unit retained for evidence display.
Nodal lesions must carry short axis; a nodal lesion carrying only a longest diameter is a structural finding, not a silent substitution.
Lesion identity is (subject_id, lesion_link_id). Missing or duplicated link ids are structural findings.
Assessments are grouped per (subject, visit, evaluator). Each evaluator stream is derived independently.
Dates are ISO-8601; partial dates are retained as partial and rules that need full precision declare themselves not evaluable for that record.

contract.description: The agent's output unit, consumed by the web application and by exports. Stable across releases; additive changes only within a MAJOR version.

Reason of the issue and background

processingPipeline.stage: Parse and validate source extracts against TEA-CTR-001; normalise units and dates; resolve lesion identity; emit family ST findings for structural defects. A study with structural defects still proceeds; affected subjects are marked partially evaluable.

Resolve the effective parameter set: guideline profile defaults overridden by protocol configuration. Compute protocol_config_hash. Determine which rules are applicable and which are deactivated for missing required fields; record both in the coverage report.
Compute DerivedTimepoint for every assessment in visit-date order per evaluator stream, then DerivedSubjectSummary. Populate derivation_trace for every computed value.
Execute applicable rules. Each rule returns zero or more raw findings carrying structured evidence and a dedupe key. Rules are independent; execution order does not affect results.

For rules declaring llmAssist mode="adjudicate", call the model with the evidence envelope and a strict output schema. A rule's deterministic trigger is never overturned; the adjudication may only set confidence, add rationale, or downgrade severity to INFO when the rule declares downgradeable="true".
Classify each finding against the query history (see ).
Render the five reviewer-facing elements. Numeric values are injected from evidence by the template engine after generation, never trusted from model output.
Persist run, findings, coverage report and provenance; expose via API; produce exports.
Accept reviewer dispositions; maintain the audit trail; make dispositions available to the next run for suppression and recurrence detection.
processingPipeline.errorPolicy: A failure in stages 5 or 8 degrades to deterministic behaviour for the affected findings and is recorded in the run log; it never aborts the run. A failure in stages 1–4 aborts the run with a diagnostic, because partial deterministic results would be misleading.

derivations.note: These functions are the foundation of the whole system and carry the highest test rigour. All are pure: (canonical model, config) → values. No I/O, no model calls.

function.name: sumOfDiameters
function.logic: contributions = [] for lesion in targetLesions: # baseline-selected targets only m = measurement(assessment, lesion) if m is None or m.state in (NOT_EVALUABLE, NOT_DONE): complete = false contributions.append((lesion, null, m.state)) continue if m.state == ABSENT: value = 0 elif m.state == TOO_SMALL_TO_MEASURE: value = config.too_small_to_measure_default_mm else: value = m.value_mm # short axis if nodal contributions.append((lesion, value, m.state)) sum_mm = sum(v for (_, v, _) in contributions if v is not null) return (sum_mm, complete, contributions)

notes.note: Nodal target lesions always contribute their short axis, including when below 10 mm (ID-03).
`complete=false` means the sum is a partial sum; downstream logic must not use it for PR/SD conclusions, only for a PD conclusion when the partial sum already crosses the threshold (ID-04).

function.name: nadir
function.logic: candidates = [a for a in assessmentsUpTo # includes baseline, includes current if a.derived.sum_complete == true and a.derived.sum_of_diameters is not null] if candidates is empty: return (null, null) pick the minimum sum_of_diameters; ties resolve to the earliest assessment_date

notes.note: Only complete sums are eligible to become the nadir; a partial sum could understate the true burden and produce a spurious PD later.
The nadir is recomputed at each timepoint from all prior timepoints including the current one, per RECIST 1.1 ("smallest sum on study").

function.name: percentChanges
function.logic: pct_from_baseline = (sum - baselineSum) / baselineSum * 100 if baselineSum > 0 else null pct_from_nadir = (sum - nadirSum) / nadirSum * 100 if nadirSum > 0 else null abs_from_nadir_mm = sum - nadirSum # Special case: nadirSum == 0 (all targets resolved). Any measurable regrowth is handled by # the absolute-increase criterion and by the new/reappeared-lesion path; percent change is null # and must not be reported as infinite.

function.name: targetResponse
function.signature: targetResponse(derived, baselineSum, nadirSum, contributions, config) → code
function.logic:
if no target lesions at baseline: return NOT_APPLICABLE
pd_by_sum = (sum_complete or partialSumAlreadyExceeds) and pct_from_nadir >= config.pd_relative_increase_pct and abs_from_nadir_mm >= config.pd_absolute_increase_mm # 5 mm in RECIST 1.1, 0 in 1.0 if pd_by_sum: return PD
if not sum_complete: return NE # ID-04: cannot exclude PR/SD/CR with missing data
all_non_nodal_absent = every non-nodal target has state ABSENT all_nodal_below_threshold = every nodal target has value < config.pathological_node_threshold_mm if all_non_nodal_absent and all_nodal_below_threshold: return CR
if pct_from_baseline <= -config.pr_decrease_pct: return PR
return SD

notes.note: CR requires the disappearance of all non-nodal target lesions AND reduction of every pathological node (target or non-target) to below 10 mm short axis. The non-target part of that condition is enforced in D-05 and in rule TE-RS-004.
TOO_SMALL_TO_MEASURE is not ABSENT and therefore blocks CR.
`partialSumAlreadyExceeds` = the sum over measured lesions alone, treating unmeasured lesions as 0, already meets both PD criteria.

function.name: nonTargetResponse
function.logic: states = [measurement(assessment, l).non_target_state for l in nonTargetLesions] if any state == UNEQUIVOCAL_PROGRESSION: return PD if any state == NOT_EVALUABLE and no state == UNEQUIVOCAL_PROGRESSION: return NE if every state == ABSENT and every pathological node among non-targets is < config.pathological_node_threshold_mm and (not config.tumor_markers_used_for_cr or all markers within normal limits): return CR return NON_CR_NON_PD

function.name: newLesionStatus
function.signature: newLesionStatus(assessment, lesions, config) → YES | NO | EQUIVOCAL
function.logic: newAtThisVisit = [l for l in lesions if l.category == NEW and l.identified_at == assessment.id] if any l in newAtThisVisit flagged unequivocal: return YES if any l in newAtThisVisit flagged equivocal: return EQUIVOCAL # -> contributes NE, not PD return NO

notes.note: A lesion in an anatomical region not imaged at baseline still counts as new; rule TE-RS-011 checks that this was considered rather than assumed.
Equivocal findings are re-assessed at the next timepoint; if confirmed, progression is dated to the first observation (rule TE-RS-013).

function.name: overallTimepointResponse
function.logic:
if newLesion == YES: return PD if target == PD or nonTarget == PD: return PD
if hasMeasurableDisease: # RECIST 1.1 overall response table, subjects WITH measurable disease at baseline (CR, CR) -> CR (CR, NON_CR_NON_PD) -> PR (CR, NE) -> PR (PR, NON_CR_NON_PD|NE) -> PR (SD, NON_CR_NON_PD|NE) -> SD (NE, non-PD) -> NE else: # subjects with NON-TARGET disease only nonTarget == CR -> CR nonTarget == NON_CR_NON_PD -> NON_CR_NON_PD nonTarget == NE -> NE

notes.note: PR and SD are not assignable to a subject without measurable disease at baseline. Rule TE-RS-016 detects this common error.
An equivocal new lesion maps to newLesion=EQUIVOCAL, which yields NE rather than PD unless target or non-target independently give PD.

function.name: bestOverallResponse
function.logic:
considered = timepoints from first dose up to and including the first PD timepoint (later timepoints excluded, ID-07)
if not config.response_confirmation_required: bor = best of considered by rank CR > PR > SD > NON_CR_NON_PD > PD > NE # SD requires the minimum interval from baseline when config.sd_min_duration_days is set; # an SD earlier than that becomes NE for BOR purposes. else: # Confirmation required: a CR or PR must be repeated at a subsequent assessment # at least config.confirmation_min_interval_days later. CR then CR -> CR CR then PR -> PR or SD or PD, per the RECIST 1.1 confirmation table; the first CR is treated as erroneous, so any residual disease at the later timepoint is judged against baseline CR then SD / PD / NE -> SD if the SD minimum duration is met, else PD or NE PR then CR -> PR PR then PR -> PR PR then SD -> SD PR then PD / NE -> SD if the SD minimum duration is met, else PD or NE NE then NE -> NE confirmation_status = CONFIRMED | UNCONFIRMED

notes.note: Confirmation is required only where the protocol requires it, typically single-arm trials with response as the primary endpoint. Configuration governs; see OQ-04.
The supporting timepoints are recorded so the UI can show exactly which two assessments produced a confirmed response.

function.name: irecistStateMachine
function.signature: irecistStateMachine(orderedTimepoints, config) → sequence of iRECIST states
function.logic:
state = NO_PROGRESSION for tp in orderedTimepoints: r11 = tp.overall_response_derived # RECIST 1.1 result for this timepoint if state == NO_PROGRESSION: if r11 == PD: state = iUPD record driver = {TARGET | NON_TARGET | NEW_LESION} (may be several) record reference values at iUPD: target sum, non-target extent, new-lesion sum else: state = map(r11): CR->iCR, PR->iPR, SD->iSD, NE->iNE elif state == iUPD: # Confirmation window check is a rule, not part of the state machine. confirmed = false if TARGET in driver and tp.sum_of_diameters >= iUPD.sum + config.icpd_target_increment_mm: confirmed = true if NON_TARGET in driver and tp.non_target shows any further unequivocal worsening: confirmed = true if NEW_LESION in driver and (tp.new_lesion_sum >= iUPD.new_lesion_sum + config.icpd_new_lesion_increment_mm or additional new lesions appeared or new non-target lesions worsened): confirmed = true # A NEW progression driver appearing for the first time at this timepoint also confirms. if a driver not present at iUPD now meets RECIST 1.1 PD criteria: confirmed = true
if confirmed: state = iCPD; stop else: # reset: burden stable or improved state = map(r11): CR->iCR, PR->iPR, SD->iSD, NE->iNE # nadir is unchanged; a later increase is measured against the original nadir, # so a subsequent iUPD is possible and permitted.

notes.note: New lesions under iRECIST are recorded and summed SEPARATELY from the baseline target sum (up to 5 new target lesions, 2 per organ). They are never added to the baseline sum. Rule TE-IR-004 detects the error.
iCPD is terminal for response derivation; assessments after it are retained but excluded from iBOR.
Continuation of treatment beyond iUPD requires the subject to be clinically stable; the documentation check is rule TE-IR-008.

function.name: progressionDate
function.logic: PD date = assessment_date of the earliest timepoint meeting PD criteria (for an equivocal new lesion later confirmed: the date of the FIRST observation) For iRECIST, the progression date for analysis is the iCPD date, while the iUPD date is retained for sensitivity analyses. Both are reported.

conventions.convention: Rule id format: TE-{FAMILY}-{NNN}. Ids are permanent; a retired rule keeps its id and is marked RETIRED.

Placeholders in message templates use {curly_braces} and are filled from the evidence object by the template engine. The LLM may rephrase around them but the engine re-injects the values after generation.
`severity` is the default; the query reconciler may escalate by one level for ANSWERED_UNRESOLVED, and adjudication may downgrade to INFO where downgradeable="true".
Every rule declares `requiredFields`; if any is absent from the study extract the rule is deactivated and listed in the coverage report as NOT_EVALUATED with the reason.

rule.title: Lesion measured at follow-up but not identified at baseline or as a new lesion
rule.intent: Every measurement must belong to a lesion with a known identity and category.
rule.logic: for m in measurements: if m.lesion_id not in lesions: raise finding

messages.reviewPoint: Referential integrity between tumor measurement records and tumor identification records.
messages.issue: Subject {subject_id}, {visit}: a measurement of {value} mm is recorded for lesion {lesion_id}, but no corresponding lesion identification record exists.
messages.reason: Measurements can only be interpreted against an identified lesion with a category (target/non-target/new) and location. Without it, the lesion cannot enter the sum of diameters, and the derived response may be wrong.
messages.query: A measurement is recorded for lesion {lesion_id} at {visit} but this lesion is not present on the tumor identification form. Please confirm the lesion identification and complete the missing record, or correct the lesion number on the measurement.
messages.tips: Most often a lesion numbering typo, or a new lesion measured before it was formally recorded as new. Check whether the number matches an existing lesion at another site of disease.

rule.title: Duplicate lesion identity
rule.intent: The same anatomical lesion must not be recorded twice.
rule.logic: group lesions by (subject, organ, laterality, normalised location_detail) if group size > 1 and both are TARGET or both NON_TARGET: raise finding

messages.reviewPoint: Duplicate recording of the same lesion under two lesion numbers.
messages.issue: Subject {subject_id}: lesions {lesion_id_a} and {lesion_id_b} are both recorded as {category} at {organ} {laterality} ({location_a} / {location_b}).
messages.reason: If the same lesion is recorded twice, it is counted twice in the sum of diameters, inflating tumor burden and distorting percent change and the nadir.
messages.query: Lesions {lesion_id_a} and {lesion_id_b} appear to describe the same lesion at {organ}. Please confirm whether these are two distinct lesions; if not, please remove the duplicate and update the affected assessments.
messages.tips: Compare the baseline sizes and the size trajectory: identical or near-identical values across visits strongly suggests duplication.

rule.title: Nodal lesion recorded without a short axis
rule.intent: Nodal lesions must be measured in short axis; a longest diameter cannot substitute.
rule.logic: if lesion.is_nodal and measurement provides only longest diameter: raise finding

messages.reviewPoint: Measurement axis for lymph node lesions.
messages.issue: Subject {subject_id}, {visit}, lesion {lesion_id} ({organ} node): the recorded measurement appears to be a longest diameter rather than a short axis.
messages.reason: RECIST 1.1 requires the short axis for nodal lesions, at baseline and at every follow-up. Using the longest diameter overstates the nodal contribution to the sum and can mask a response or create a false progression.
messages.query: Lesion {lesion_id} is a lymph node. Please confirm the measurement recorded at {visit} is the short axis; if the longest diameter was recorded, please correct it.
messages.tips: Nodal lesions were only formally distinguished from RECIST 1.0 onwards in version 1.1; sites experienced with older studies frequently record the long axis out of habit.

rule.title: Unit or precision inconsistency
rule.intent: Detect mixed cm/mm entry and implausible precision.
rule.logic: if original_unit differs within a subject, or a value is < 1 with unit mm, or a non-nodal target value > 300 mm: raise finding

messages.reviewPoint: Consistency of measurement units and precision across a subject's records.
messages.issue: Subject {subject_id}: measurements are recorded in {units_seen}; lesion {lesion_id} at {visit} has value {original_value} {original_unit}.
messages.reason: A centimetre value entered in a millimetre field understates a lesion tenfold, which can convert a progression into an apparent response.
messages.query: Please confirm the unit of the measurement for lesion {lesion_id} at {visit} ({original_value} {original_unit}); the value appears inconsistent with the other measurements recorded for this subject.
messages.tips: Check the trajectory of the same lesion across visits — a tenfold step between adjacent visits is diagnostic of a unit error.

rule.title: Assessment visit sequence and date order inconsistent
rule.intent: Visit numbering and assessment dates must be monotonic.
rule.logic: order assessments by visit_number; if assessment_date is not non-decreasing: raise finding

messages.reviewPoint: Chronological consistency of tumor assessment visits.
messages.issue: Subject {subject_id}: {visit_a} ({date_a}) is dated after {visit_b} ({date_b}) although it precedes it in the visit sequence.
messages.reason: Nadir, progression dating and best overall response all depend on chronological order. An out-of-order date can move the nadir and change the progression determination.
messages.query: The assessment dates for {visit_a} and {visit_b} appear inconsistent with the visit sequence. Please verify the assessment dates.
messages.tips: Confirm against the scan dates in the imaging report rather than the visit date, which may reflect the clinic visit rather than the scan.

rule.title: Number of target lesions exceeds the maximum
rule.intent: Target lesion count must not exceed the guideline/protocol maximum.
rule.logic: n = count(lesions where category == TARGET and identified at baseline) if n > config.max_target_lesions_total: raise finding

messages.reviewPoint: Maximum number of target lesions permitted at baseline.
messages.issue: Subject {subject_id}: {n} target lesions are recorded at baseline; the maximum permitted is {max_total}.
messages.reason: RECIST {guideline_version} permits a maximum of {max_total} target lesions in total. Additional lesions must be recorded as non-target. Including extra lesions in the sum changes the denominator for percent change and can alter the response category at every subsequent timepoint.
messages.query: {n} target lesions are recorded at baseline for this subject, exceeding the maximum of {max_total} specified in the protocol. Please review the target lesion selection and re-classify the excess lesions as non-target, updating all affected assessments.
messages.tips: Re-selection changes the baseline sum and therefore every subsequent percent change; expect all downstream responses to require re-derivation. Prioritise this issue before reviewing any response mismatch for this subject.

rule.title: Target lesions per organ exceeds the maximum
rule.intent: No more than the permitted number of target lesions may be selected from any one organ.
rule.logic: for organ, group in targets grouped by organ: if count(group) > config.max_target_lesions_per_organ: raise finding

messages.reviewPoint: Maximum number of target lesions per organ.
messages.issue: Subject {subject_id}: {n} target lesions are recorded in {organ}; the maximum permitted per organ is {max_per_organ}.
messages.reason: RECIST {guideline_version} limits target lesions to {max_per_organ} per organ so that the sum represents the overall disease burden rather than one organ. Over-representation of one organ biases the response assessment.
messages.query: {n} target lesions are recorded in {organ}, exceeding the per-organ maximum of {max_per_organ}. Please re-classify the excess lesions as non-target and update the affected assessments.
messages.tips: Lymph nodes in different nodal stations are commonly all coded to a single "lymph node" organ; confirm whether the sponsor's convention treats nodal stations as separate organs before raising.

rule.title: Non-nodal target lesion below the measurability threshold at baseline
rule.intent: Target lesions must be measurable at baseline.
rule.logic: for t in non-nodal targets: threshold = config.min_measurable_non_nodal_mm if method == CXR: threshold = config.min_measurable_cxr_mm if method == CLINICAL_EXAM: threshold = config.min_measurable_clinical_exam_mm if baseline value < threshold: raise finding

messages.reviewPoint: Measurability of selected target lesions at baseline.
messages.issue: Subject {subject_id}: target lesion {lesion_id} ({organ}) measures {value} mm at baseline by {method}, below the {threshold} mm minimum for a measurable lesion.
messages.reason: RECIST {guideline_version} requires a non-nodal lesion to be at least {threshold} mm by {method} to be measurable and therefore eligible as a target lesion. Sub-threshold lesions are subject to unreliable measurement, and including one makes the whole sum unreliable.
messages.query: Target lesion {lesion_id} measures {value} mm at baseline, below the {threshold} mm threshold for measurability by {method}. Please confirm the measurement, or re-classify this lesion as non-target and update the affected assessments.
messages.tips: Check the imaging slice thickness where available: a lesion must be at least twice the slice thickness to be measurable, so a 10 mm lesion on 8 mm slices is not measurable even though it meets the nominal threshold.

rule.title: Nodal target lesion with baseline short axis below 15 mm
rule.intent: Only nodes with short axis at least 15 mm are eligible as target lesions.
rule.logic: for t in nodal targets: if baseline short axis < config.min_measurable_nodal_short_axis_mm: raise finding

messages.reviewPoint: Eligibility of lymph nodes as target lesions (short axis ≥ 15 mm).
messages.issue: Subject {subject_id}: nodal target lesion {lesion_id} ({organ}) has a baseline short axis of {value} mm, below the 15 mm requirement.
messages.reason: RECIST 1.1 requires a short axis of at least 15 mm for a node to be measurable and selectable as a target lesion. Nodes with a short axis of 10 to under 15 mm are pathological but non-measurable and should be recorded as non-target; nodes under 10 mm are non-pathological and should not be recorded at all.
messages.query: Nodal target lesion {lesion_id} has a baseline short axis of {value} mm. Please confirm the measurement; a node with short axis below 15 mm should be recorded as a non-target lesion (10 to <15 mm) or not recorded (<10 mm).
messages.tips: This is one of the most frequent baseline errors. Verify that the recorded value is a short axis and not a longest diameter before concluding the selection was wrong.

tests.test: short axis exactly 15 mm → no finding
short axis 12 mm as target → finding

rule.title: Non-pathological node recorded as a lesion
rule.intent: Nodes with short axis below 10 mm are not pathological and should not be recorded.
rule.logic: for l in nodal lesions (target or non-target): if baseline short axis < config.pathological_node_threshold_mm: raise finding

messages.reviewPoint: Recording of lymph nodes that do not meet the pathological threshold.
messages.issue: Subject {subject_id}: node {lesion_id} ({organ}) has a baseline short axis of {value} mm and is recorded as a {category} lesion.
messages.reason: Under RECIST 1.1 a node with a short axis below 10 mm is considered non-pathological and is not recorded or followed. Recording it adds normal tissue to the disease assessment and can prevent a complete response from being assigned.
messages.query: Node {lesion_id} has a baseline short axis of {value} mm, below the 10 mm pathological threshold. Please confirm whether this node should be recorded as disease; if not, please remove it from the assessment.
messages.tips: Where a node is clinically relevant despite being below threshold (for example biopsy-proven involvement), the site should document the rationale; consider accepting with a comment rather than a data change.

rule.title: Lesion size below twice the imaging slice thickness
rule.intent: Measurability depends on slice thickness, not only on the nominal threshold.
rule.logic: if lesion is target and baseline value < 2 * slice_thickness_mm: raise finding

messages.reviewPoint: Lesion measurability relative to the imaging slice thickness.
messages.issue: Subject {subject_id}: target lesion {lesion_id} measures {value} mm at baseline on {method} with {slice_thickness} mm slices.
messages.reason: RECIST 1.1 requires a lesion to be at least twice the slice thickness to be measurable; on {slice_thickness} mm slices the minimum measurable lesion is {min_size} mm. Below that, apparent size changes may be partial-volume artefacts rather than real change.
messages.query: Target lesion {lesion_id} measures {value} mm at baseline on images with {slice_thickness} mm slice thickness. Please confirm the lesion is measurable per the imaging manual, or re-classify it as non-target.
messages.tips: Slice thickness often varies between the baseline and follow-up scans; if so, the comparison itself is compromised and merits a note to the imaging vendor.

rule.title: Non-measurable disease type selected as a target lesion
rule.intent: Presentations that are non-measurable by definition must not be target lesions.
rule.logic: deterministic pre-filter: organ or location text matches a non-measurable pattern (ascites, pleural effusion, pericardial effusion, leptomeningeal disease, lymphangitic lung/skin involvement, inflammatory breast disease, simple cyst, blastic bone lesion without soft tissue component, abdominal mass identified only by physical examination) then LLM adjudication over the free text confirms or rejects, returning {is_non_measurable: bool, category: string, confidence: 0..1, rationale: string} raise finding when confirmed; confidence < 0.6 → emit as INFO

messages.reviewPoint: Selection of lesion types that RECIST classifies as non-measurable.
messages.issue: Subject {subject_id}: target lesion {lesion_id} is described as "{location_detail}" in {organ}, which appears to be {non_measurable_category}.
messages.reason: RECIST classifies {non_measurable_category} as non-measurable disease: it cannot be reproducibly measured in one dimension. Such disease must be recorded as non-target and assessed qualitatively. A non-measurable lesion inside the target sum makes the sum, and every percent change derived from it, unreliable.
messages.query: Target lesion {lesion_id} is described as "{location_detail}". This appears to represent non-measurable disease under RECIST. Please confirm the lesion selection and, if appropriate, re-classify it as a non-target lesion.
messages.tips: Blastic bone lesions are non-measurable, but a lytic or mixed lytic-blastic lesion with an identifiable soft tissue component can be measurable on CT/MRI. Cystic metastases can be measurable, but where non-cystic lesions are available they are preferred as targets.

rule.title: Previously irradiated lesion selected as target without documented progression
rule.intent: Lesions in a previously irradiated field are non-measurable unless progression after radiotherapy is documented.
rule.logic: if lesion.category == TARGET and (lesion.previously_irradiated or radiotherapy field overlaps lesion site prior to baseline) and not documented progression after radiotherapy: raise finding

messages.reviewPoint: Eligibility of lesions within a prior radiotherapy field as target lesions.
messages.issue: Subject {subject_id}: target lesion {lesion_id} ({organ}) lies in a previously irradiated field (radiotherapy {rt_date}), with no documented progression at that site after treatment.
messages.reason: RECIST treats lesions in a previously irradiated area, or subjected to other locoregional therapy, as non-measurable unless progression of that lesion has been demonstrated since the treatment. Post-radiation change can mimic both response and progression.
messages.query: Target lesion {lesion_id} is located within a prior radiotherapy field. Please confirm whether progression of this lesion has been documented since radiotherapy; if not, the lesion should be recorded as non-target.
messages.tips: Also relevant for lesions treated with ablation, embolisation or surgery during the study — see TE-XD-004 for on-study local therapy.

rule.title: No measurable disease at baseline but target lesions recorded
rule.intent: Consistency between the measurable-disease determination and target lesion recording.
rule.logic: if reported "measurable disease at baseline" == NO and count(targets) > 0: raise finding also inverse: if == YES and count(targets) == 0 and measurable lesions exist: raise finding

messages.reviewPoint: Consistency between the baseline measurable disease flag and the recorded target lesions.
messages.issue: Subject {subject_id}: measurable disease at baseline is recorded as {flag}, but {n} target lesions are recorded.
messages.reason: The measurable-disease determination drives the response algorithm: subjects without measurable disease can only be assigned CR, Non-CR/Non-PD, PD or NE, never PR or SD. An inconsistency here produces a systematically wrong response for every timepoint, and may also affect eligibility.
messages.query: Measurable disease at baseline is recorded as {flag} while {n} target lesions are entered. Please confirm the baseline disease status and correct the inconsistent record.
messages.tips: Check eligibility criteria: if the protocol requires measurable disease, this may also be an eligibility deviation requiring separate escalation.

rule.title: Baseline assessment outside the protocol window relative to first dose
rule.intent: Baseline imaging must be recent enough to represent pre-treatment burden.
rule.logic: gap = first_dose_date - baseline_assessment_date if gap > config.baseline_window_days_before_first_dose or gap < 0: raise finding

messages.reviewPoint: Timing of the baseline tumor assessment relative to first dose.
messages.issue: Subject {subject_id}: baseline assessment dated {baseline_date}, first dose {first_dose_date}, a gap of {gap} days against a permitted window of {window} days.
messages.reason: A baseline older than the protocol window may no longer represent the disease burden at the start of treatment, which biases every subsequent percent change. A baseline dated after first dose is not a baseline at all and would understate treatment effect.
messages.query: The baseline tumor assessment ({baseline_date}) falls {gap} days before first dose ({first_dose_date}), outside the protocol window of {window} days. Please confirm the assessment date and whether a protocol deviation has been recorded.
messages.tips: Distinguish the scan date from the assessment or read date; the protocol window normally applies to the scan.

rule.title: Reported baseline sum of diameters does not match the recorded lesions
rule.intent: Arithmetic verification of the baseline sum.
rule.logic: derived = sumOfDiameters(baseline, targets, config) if |reported_sum - derived.sum| > config.sum_tolerance_mm: raise finding

messages.reviewPoint: Recomputation of the baseline sum of diameters from the individual target lesion measurements.
messages.issue: Subject {subject_id}: baseline sum of diameters is reported as {reported} mm; the sum of the {n} recorded target lesions is {derived} mm (difference {difference} mm).
messages.reason: The baseline sum is the reference for every partial response determination. An error of {difference} mm shifts the 30% response threshold and can change the response category at multiple timepoints. Recorded lesions: {lesion_breakdown}.
messages.query: The baseline sum of diameters ({reported} mm) does not equal the sum of the recorded target lesion measurements ({derived} mm). Please verify the individual measurements and the sum.
messages.tips: Check first whether a nodal target was included using its longest diameter, and whether all target lesions have a baseline measurement.

rule.title: Target lesion selection not favouring the largest measurable lesions
rule.intent: Target lesions should be the largest reproducibly measurable lesions.
rule.logic: if any non-target measurable lesion at baseline is larger than the smallest target lesion by more than config.selection_margin_mm (default 5): raise finding

messages.reviewPoint: Rationality of target lesion selection relative to lesion size.
messages.issue: Subject {subject_id}: non-target lesion {nt_lesion_id} ({nt_value} mm) is larger than target lesion {t_lesion_id} ({t_value} mm).
messages.reason: RECIST directs that target lesions be selected on the basis of size, choosing the largest lesions that are reproducibly measurable, while remaining representative of all involved organs. Selecting smaller lesions as targets while larger measurable lesions are left as non-target reduces the sensitivity of the response assessment.
messages.query: Non-target lesion {nt_lesion_id} ({nt_value} mm) is larger than target lesion {t_lesion_id} ({t_value} mm). Please confirm the target lesion selection rationale, for example poor reproducibility of the larger lesion.
messages.tips: Reproducibility legitimately overrides size — a large but ill-defined or confluent mass is a poor target. Expect a proportion of these to be correctly explained rather than corrected.

rule.title: Target lesion without a baseline measurement
rule.intent: Every target lesion needs a baseline value to enter the sum.
rule.logic: for t in targets: if no baseline measurement with state PRESENT: raise finding

messages.reviewPoint: Completeness of baseline measurements for all selected target lesions.
messages.issue: Subject {subject_id}: target lesion {lesion_id} has no baseline measurement (state recorded as {state}).
messages.reason: Without a baseline value the lesion cannot contribute to the baseline sum, so the reference for percent change is understated and partial response may be reported prematurely.
messages.query: Target lesion {lesion_id} has no baseline measurement. Please enter the baseline measurement, or re-classify the lesion if it was not measurable at baseline.
messages.tips: A target lesion that was not evaluable at baseline should not have been selected as a target; check whether re-selection is required.

rule.title: Assessment method inconsistent between baseline and follow-up for the same lesion
rule.intent: The same lesion should be followed by the same modality throughout.
rule.logic: for lesion, visits in measurements grouped by lesion: if distinct method_at_visit values > 1: raise finding

messages.reviewPoint: Consistency of imaging modality for each lesion across visits.
messages.issue: Subject {subject_id}: lesion {lesion_id} is measured by {method_a} at {visit_a} and by {method_b} at {visit_b}.
messages.reason: RECIST requires the same method of assessment and the same technique at baseline and during follow-up. Different modalities measure different things — a change of modality can produce an apparent size change of the order of the response thresholds without any true biological change.
messages.query: Lesion {lesion_id} was assessed by {method_a} at baseline and {method_b} at {visit_b}. Please confirm the modality used and whether the change was clinically necessary.
messages.tips: Where a modality change was unavoidable, the affected timepoint may need to be treated as not evaluable for that lesion rather than measured.

rule.title: Baseline scans span more days than permitted
rule.intent: All baseline imaging should represent a single point in time.
rule.logic: span = max(scan_dates) - min(scan_dates) if span > config.scan_span_max_days: raise finding

messages.reviewPoint: Temporal coherence of the scans composing a single tumor assessment.
messages.issue: Subject {subject_id}, {visit}: scans span {span} days ({earliest} to {latest}), exceeding the permitted {max_span} days.
messages.reason: An assessment is intended to be a snapshot. When component scans are widely separated, lesions measured on the later scans reflect a different point in the disease course, which distorts the sum and, at baseline, the reference for all later comparisons.
messages.query: The scans comprising the {visit} tumor assessment span {span} days. Please confirm the scan dates and whether all scans belong to this assessment.
messages.tips: Commonly caused by brain MRI scheduled separately from body CT; confirm the imaging manual's tolerance before raising.

rule.title: Lesion location inconsistent with the assigned organ or laterality
rule.intent: Detect coding errors between the free-text location and the coded organ/laterality.
rule.logic: LLM classifies (organ, laterality, location_detail) as consistent / inconsistent / unclear with rationale; only "inconsistent" with confidence >= 0.7 raises a finding

messages.reviewPoint: Anatomical consistency between the coded organ, laterality and the free-text lesion description.
messages.issue: Subject {subject_id}: lesion {lesion_id} is coded to {organ} {laterality} but described as "{location_detail}".
messages.reason: Organ coding drives the per-organ target lesion limit and the interpretation of new lesions by region. A mismatch can hide a breach of the per-organ limit or misclassify a new lesion.
messages.query: Lesion {lesion_id} is recorded at {organ} {laterality} with the description "{location_detail}". Please confirm the anatomical location and correct the coding if needed.
messages.tips: Laterality errors are the most common subtype and matter most for paired organs (lung, kidney, breast, adnexa).

rule.title: Baseline assessment missing entirely while follow-up assessments exist
rule.intent: No follow-up can be interpreted without a baseline.
rule.logic: if subject has follow-up assessments and no assessment flagged is_baseline: raise finding

messages.reviewPoint: Presence of a baseline tumor assessment for every subject with follow-up data.
messages.issue: Subject {subject_id}: {n} follow-up tumor assessments are recorded but no baseline assessment exists.
messages.reason: Percent change from baseline, the nadir and every response category depend on a baseline. Without it the subject cannot contribute to any efficacy endpoint.
messages.query: No baseline tumor assessment is recorded for this subject although follow-up assessments exist. Please enter the baseline assessment or confirm why it was not performed.
messages.tips: Check whether the baseline was entered under a screening visit name that failed to map; this is frequently a data-transfer issue rather than missing data.

rule.title: Reported sum of diameters does not match the recorded lesions at a follow-up visit
rule.intent: Arithmetic verification of the sum at every timepoint.

messages.reviewPoint: Recomputation of the sum of diameters at each timepoint from the individual target lesion measurements.
messages.issue: Subject {subject_id}, {visit}: sum of diameters reported as {reported} mm; recomputed from the {n} target lesions as {derived} mm (difference {difference} mm). Lesion contributions: {lesion_breakdown}.
messages.reason: The sum drives percent change from baseline (partial response) and from nadir (progression). A {difference} mm error at this timepoint changes the percent change from {reported_pct}% to {derived_pct}% and the derived response from {reported_response} to {derived_response}.
messages.query: The sum of diameters recorded at {visit} ({reported} mm) does not match the sum of the individual target lesion measurements ({derived} mm). Please verify the individual measurements and the recorded sum.
messages.tips: Check for a lesion measured but omitted from the sum, a lesion recorded as absent but still included, and nodal lesions entered with the wrong axis.

rule.title: Target lesion measurement missing without a not-done reason
rule.intent: Missing data must be explained, not silent.
rule.logic: if measurement absent or value null and state not in (ABSENT, TOO_SMALL_TO_MEASURE, NOT_EVALUABLE, NOT_DONE) or state in (NOT_EVALUABLE, NOT_DONE) with no reason recorded: raise finding

messages.reviewPoint: Completeness and explanation of missing target lesion measurements.
messages.issue: Subject {subject_id}, {visit}: target lesion {lesion_id} has no measurement and no reason recorded.
messages.reason: An unexplained missing measurement makes the sum incomplete, which forces the target response to not evaluable and can propagate into a missing timepoint for progression-free survival.
messages.query: No measurement is recorded for target lesion {lesion_id} at {visit}. Please enter the measurement or record the reason it could not be assessed.
messages.tips: Distinguish "not evaluable" (lesion could not be assessed) from "absent" (lesion no longer visible); the two have opposite consequences for response.

rule.title: Target response reported despite an unevaluable target lesion
rule.intent: Enforce the not-evaluable rule with its progression exception.

messages.reviewPoint: Handling of not-evaluable target lesions in the timepoint response.
messages.issue: Subject {subject_id}, {visit}: target lesion {lesion_id} is not evaluable, yet the target response is reported as {reported_response}.
messages.reason: When any target lesion cannot be assessed, the sum is incomplete and the true tumor burden is unknown, so the response is not evaluable. The exception is progression: if the measured lesions alone already meet the progression threshold, progressive disease can still be assigned. Here the measured lesions sum to {partial_sum} mm against a nadir of {nadir} mm ({partial_pct}%), which does not reach the progression threshold.
messages.query: Target lesion {lesion_id} is recorded as not evaluable at {visit} while the target lesion response is reported as {reported_response}. Please confirm; where a target lesion cannot be assessed, the target response should normally be not evaluable.
messages.tips: This is a systematic misunderstanding at many sites: a lesion that is "not seen because it resolved" should be recorded as absent, not as not evaluable.

rule.title: Implausible measurement change for a single lesion
rule.intent: Outlier detection on lesion trajectories.

messages.reviewPoint: Plausibility of the change in an individual lesion between consecutive assessments.
messages.issue: Subject {subject_id}: lesion {lesion_id} changes from {prev_value} mm at {prev_visit} to {value} mm at {visit} ({pct_delta}% over {interval} days).
messages.reason: A change of this magnitude over {interval} days is unusual and is more often a transcription error, a unit error, or measurement of a different lesion than true biology. The change moves the sum from {prev_sum} mm to {sum} mm and the derived response from {prev_response} to {response}.
messages.query: Lesion {lesion_id} changed from {prev_value} mm to {value} mm between {prev_visit} and {visit}. Please verify the measurement against the imaging report.
messages.tips: Genuine large changes do occur — rapid response to targeted therapy, cavitation, haemorrhage into a lesion, or coalescence of adjacent lesions. Look for a comment or a matching change in a neighbouring lesion.

rule.title: Lesion recorded as absent and subsequently measured again
rule.intent: Detect and correctly handle reappearance of a resolved lesion.

messages.reviewPoint: Handling of a target lesion that disappeared and later reappeared.
messages.issue: Subject {subject_id}: lesion {lesion_id} was recorded as absent at {absent_visit} and measures {value} mm at {visit}.
messages.reason: A previously resolved target lesion that reappears re-enters the sum of diameters at its measured size; it is not a new lesion, because it was present at baseline. Progression is then judged against the nadir. If it has instead been recorded as a new lesion, progression will be dated incorrectly and the sum will double-count the disease.
messages.query: Lesion {lesion_id} was recorded as absent at {absent_visit} and is measured again at {visit}. Please confirm this is the same baseline target lesion rather than a new lesion, and that it is included in the sum of diameters.
messages.tips: Confirm the protocol's position: some protocols treat reappearance after a complete response as progression in itself. The study configuration setting is reappearance_is_progression = {reappearance_is_progression}.

rule.title: Inconsistent use of the too-small-to-measure convention
rule.intent: One convention per study.
rule.logic: if the study contains both TOO_SMALL_TO_MEASURE states and lesions recorded with the default value (e.g. 5 mm) under state PRESENT: raise finding at study level

messages.reviewPoint: Consistency of the convention for lesions that are visible but too small to measure reliably.
messages.issue: Study {study_id}: {n_state} records use the too-small-to-measure state while {n_value} records appear to use a fixed {default} mm value under a present state ({examples}).
messages.reason: The two conventions produce different sums and different eligibility for complete response. Mixing them makes cross-subject comparison unreliable and can make a complete response unassignable for some subjects and assignable for others with identical imaging.
messages.query: Please confirm the convention used for lesions below the limit of reliable measurement at this site, so that the records can be harmonised.
messages.tips: Agree the convention centrally and document it in the imaging manual; retrospective harmonisation is usually preferable to leaving the study mixed.

rule.title: Assessment interval outside the protocol schedule
rule.intent: Assessments must follow the protocol calendar so that progression dating is comparable.
rule.logic: for consecutive assessments: if |interval - config.assessment_interval_days| > config.assessment_window_days: raise finding

messages.reviewPoint: Compliance of tumor assessment timing with the protocol-defined schedule and window.
messages.issue: Subject {subject_id}: {interval} days between {prev_visit} ({prev_date}) and {visit} ({date}); the protocol specifies {expected} ± {window} days.
messages.reason: Assessment timing determines the resolution of progression dating and, in randomised trials, the comparability of progression-free survival between arms. Systematically late assessments delay progression detection.
messages.query: The interval between {prev_visit} and {visit} is {interval} days, outside the protocol window of {expected} ± {window} days. Please confirm the assessment date and whether a protocol deviation has been recorded.
messages.tips: Cluster by site: isolated deviations are scheduling reality, but a site with a consistent bias is a monitoring signal.

rule.title: Missing scheduled assessment before progression or censoring
rule.intent: Detect gaps that affect progression-free survival censoring.
rule.logic: if gap between assessments >= 2 * config.assessment_interval_days and subject still on treatment during the gap: raise finding

messages.reviewPoint: Continuity of tumor assessments while the subject remains on study.
messages.issue: Subject {subject_id}: no tumor assessment between {prev_date} and {date}, a gap of {gap} days spanning approximately {n_missed} scheduled assessments while the subject remained on treatment.
messages.reason: Two or more consecutively missed assessments typically require censoring at the last evaluable assessment in progression-free survival analyses, which reduces the information contributed by this subject and can bias the estimate.
messages.query: No tumor assessment is recorded between {prev_date} and {date} although the subject remained on treatment. Please confirm whether assessments were performed and, if so, enter the data; otherwise please record the reason.
messages.tips: Cross-check against the visit schedule and any unscheduled visits; assessments performed but entered under an unmapped visit name are a common cause.

rule.title: Nodal target lesion recorded as absent or zero
rule.intent: Nodes remain measurable and stay in the sum even when they normalise.
rule.logic: if lesion.is_nodal and lesion.category == TARGET and (state == ABSENT or value == 0): raise finding

messages.reviewPoint: Treatment of nodal target lesions that shrink below the pathological threshold.
messages.issue: Subject {subject_id}, {visit}: nodal target lesion {lesion_id} ({organ}) is recorded as {state_or_zero}.
messages.reason: Under RECIST 1.1 lymph nodes always retain a measurable short axis and are never recorded as absent; they continue to contribute their short axis to the sum even when it falls below 10 mm. The sum therefore need not reach zero for a complete response — what is required is that every pathological node has a short axis below 10 mm. Recording the node as zero understates the sum by its true short axis and can produce a false partial response or complete response.
messages.query: Nodal target lesion {lesion_id} is recorded as {state_or_zero} at {visit}. Lymph nodes should continue to be measured in short axis at every visit, including when they normalise. Please enter the measured short axis.
messages.tips: This is the single most common nodal error and it usually reflects a well-intentioned attempt to make the arithmetic produce a complete response. Explain the rule to the site rather than only requesting the correction.

tests.test: nodal target with state ABSENT at cycle 4 → finding
nodal target measuring 7 mm short axis → no finding

rule.title: Non-target lesion state missing at a follow-up assessment
rule.intent: Non-target lesions must be assessed qualitatively at every timepoint.
rule.logic: if non-target lesion has no non_target_state at a performed assessment: raise finding

messages.reviewPoint: Completeness of qualitative non-target lesion assessment at each timepoint.
messages.issue: Subject {subject_id}, {visit}: no assessment is recorded for non-target lesion {lesion_id} ({organ}).
messages.reason: The non-target response contributes to the overall timepoint response, and unequivocal progression of non-target disease is sufficient for progression on its own. A missing non-target assessment leaves the overall response underdetermined.
messages.query: No assessment is recorded for non-target lesion {lesion_id} at {visit}. Please record the status of this lesion.
messages.tips: Sites often assess non-target disease collectively rather than lesion by lesion; check whether the eCRF expects a per-lesion or an overall non-target response.

rule.title: Tumor assessment recorded after death or after the end of study participation
rule.intent: Temporal plausibility against subject-level dates.
rule.logic: if assessment_date > death_date: raise CRITICAL if assessment_date > discontinuation_date + config.post_treatment_followup_days: raise MAJOR

messages.reviewPoint: Consistency of tumor assessment dates with subject disposition and vital status.
messages.issue: Subject {subject_id}: tumor assessment dated {date} at {visit}, after the recorded {reference_event} of {reference_date}.
messages.reason: An assessment dated after death or well beyond the end of follow-up indicates an error in one of the two dates. Either error affects analysis: an incorrect assessment date can move the progression date, and an incorrect death date affects survival analysis.
messages.query: The {visit} tumor assessment is dated {date}, after the recorded {reference_event} ({reference_date}). Please verify both dates.
messages.tips: Post-treatment follow-up assessments are legitimate in many protocols; confirm the follow-up period before treating a post-discontinuation assessment as an error.

rule.title: New lesion recorded with an identification date earlier than the visit at which it was first reported
rule.intent: New lesion timing consistency.
rule.logic: if new lesion identified_at assessment date < the date of the assessment where it first appears in measurements: raise finding

messages.reviewPoint: Consistency between the date a new lesion was identified and the assessment at which it was reported.
messages.issue: Subject {subject_id}: new lesion {lesion_id} is dated {identified_date} but first appears in the assessment data at {visit} ({visit_date}).
messages.reason: The progression date is taken from the first assessment at which the new lesion was observed. An inconsistency between these dates produces the wrong progression date and therefore the wrong progression-free survival time.
messages.query: New lesion {lesion_id} has an identification date of {identified_date} but is first reported at {visit} ({visit_date}). Please confirm the date the lesion was first observed.
messages.tips: Where the lesion was visible in retrospect on an earlier scan, the progression date is normally the earlier scan; this requires a documented radiology decision.

rule.title: Follow-up scans span more days than permitted
rule.intent: Same coherence check as TE-BL-015, applied to follow-up assessments.
rule.logic: span = max(scan_dates) - min(scan_dates); if span > config.scan_span_max_days: raise finding

messages.reviewPoint: Temporal coherence of the scans composing a follow-up assessment.
messages.issue: Subject {subject_id}, {visit}: component scans span {span} days ({earliest} to {latest}).
messages.reason: Widely separated component scans mean that different parts of the tumor burden are measured at different times, which affects the sum and may affect the progression date.
messages.query: The scans comprising the {visit} assessment span {span} days. Please confirm the scan dates.
messages.tips: Where the span is unavoidable, the assessment date convention (earliest scan or latest scan) should be applied consistently across the study.

rule.title: Identical measurements repeated across three or more consecutive visits
rule.intent: Detect carried-forward values rather than genuine measurement.
rule.logic: if a lesion has the identical value at >= 3 consecutive assessments and the lesion is > config.identical_value_min_mm (default 15): raise finding

messages.reviewPoint: Detection of measurements that may have been carried forward rather than re-measured.
messages.issue: Subject {subject_id}: lesion {lesion_id} measures exactly {value} mm at {visits}.
messages.reason: Identical measurements of a lesion of this size across several timepoints are uncommon given normal measurement variability, and may indicate that a previous value was copied rather than the lesion re-measured. If so, the sum does not reflect the current tumor burden.
messages.query: Lesion {lesion_id} is recorded as exactly {value} mm at {visits}. Please confirm that the lesion was measured at each assessment.
messages.tips: Small and stable lesions genuinely produce repeated values; this check is deliberately informational and should be reviewed in the context of the whole subject rather than raised as a query in isolation.

rule.title: Reported target lesion response does not match the derived response
rule.intent: The central check: recompute the target response and compare.
rule.logic: derived = targetResponse(...) if reported_target_response != derived and derived is not NOT_APPLICABLE: raise finding severity CRITICAL when the mismatch changes the overall response, MAJOR otherwise

messages.reviewPoint: Derivation of the target lesion response from the sum of diameters, the baseline sum and the nadir.
messages.issue: Subject {subject_id}, {visit}: target lesion response is reported as {reported} but derives as {derived}. Sum of diameters {sum} mm; baseline {baseline_sum} mm ({pct_baseline}%); nadir {nadir_sum} mm at {nadir_visit} ({pct_nadir}%, absolute change {abs_nadir} mm).
messages.reason: {derivation_explanation}
messages.query: The target lesion response recorded at {visit} is {reported}. Based on the recorded lesion measurements the sum of diameters is {sum} mm, a {pct_baseline}% change from baseline and a {pct_nadir}% change from the nadir of {nadir_sum} mm, which corresponds to {derived}. Please review the recorded response and the underlying measurements.
messages.tips: Before querying the response, confirm the measurements themselves: a response mismatch is frequently a symptom of a measurement or sum error already flagged for this subject. Check the linked findings for this subject first.

derivationExplanationVariants.variant: The sum has increased by {pct_nadir}% from the nadir with an absolute increase of {abs_nadir} mm, meeting both the {pd_pct}% relative and the {pd_abs} mm absolute criteria for progression.
The sum has decreased by {pct_baseline_abs}% from baseline, meeting the {pr_pct}% threshold for partial response, and the increase from nadir does not meet the progression criteria.

The change from baseline ({pct_baseline}%) does not reach the {pr_pct}% decrease required for partial response, and the change from nadir ({pct_nadir}%, {abs_nadir} mm) does not meet the progression criteria.
All non-nodal target lesions are recorded as absent and all nodal target lesions have a short axis below {node_threshold} mm.
Target lesion {ne_lesion_ids} could not be assessed, so the sum is incomplete and progression cannot be established from the measured lesions alone.

tests.test: nadir 50 mm, current 60 mm (+20%, +10 mm) → PD
nadir 20 mm, current 24 mm (+20%, +4 mm) → SD, not PD
non-nodal all absent, node 8 mm → CR
non-nodal all absent, node 11 mm → PR (not CR)

rule.title: Progression declared on a relative increase without the required absolute increase
rule.intent: Enforce the 5 mm absolute criterion alongside the 20% relative criterion.
rule.logic: if reported_target_response == PD and pct_from_nadir >= config.pd_relative_increase_pct and abs_from_nadir_mm < config.pd_absolute_increase_mm: raise finding

messages.reviewPoint: Application of both progression criteria: a relative increase of at least 20% and an absolute increase of at least 5 mm from the nadir.
messages.issue: Subject {subject_id}, {visit}: progression is reported. The sum increased from a nadir of {nadir_sum} mm to {sum} mm, a {pct_nadir}% increase but only {abs_nadir} mm in absolute terms.
messages.reason: RECIST 1.1 requires both a relative increase of at least {pd_pct}% and an absolute increase of at least {pd_abs} mm from the nadir. The absolute criterion was introduced precisely for small tumor burdens, where a 20% increase can fall within measurement variability. Here the absolute increase of {abs_nadir} mm does not reach {pd_abs} mm, so the derived response is {derived}.
messages.query: Progressive disease is recorded at {visit} based on an increase from the nadir of {nadir_sum} mm to {sum} mm. This is a {pct_nadir}% increase but only {abs_nadir} mm in absolute terms, which does not meet the {pd_abs} mm absolute increase also required by RECIST 1.1. Please review the response assessment, unless progression is based on a new lesion or on unequivocal non-target progression.
messages.tips: Confirm first whether progression was actually driven by a new lesion or by non-target progression, in which case the response is correct and this finding can be rejected. This check applies only to progression driven by the target sum.

rule.title: Progression assessed against baseline rather than against the nadir
rule.intent: Detect the classic error of comparing to baseline when the tumor shrank first.
rule.logic: if reported_target_response != PD and pct_from_nadir >= pd_pct and abs_from_nadir_mm >= pd_abs and pct_from_baseline < pd_pct: raise finding

messages.reviewPoint: Use of the nadir, rather than baseline, as the reference for progression.
messages.issue: Subject {subject_id}, {visit}: target response is reported as {reported}. The sum is {sum} mm, which is {pct_baseline}% relative to baseline ({baseline_sum} mm) but {pct_nadir}% relative to the nadir of {nadir_sum} mm recorded at {nadir_visit} — an absolute increase of {abs_nadir} mm.
messages.reason: Progression is assessed against the smallest sum recorded on study, including baseline, not against baseline itself. Because this subject responded before progressing, the comparison against baseline still looks favourable while the comparison against the nadir meets the progression criteria. The derived response is progressive disease.
messages.query: At {visit} the sum of diameters is {sum} mm compared with a nadir of {nadir_sum} mm at {nadir_visit}, a {pct_nadir}% increase of {abs_nadir} mm, which meets the RECIST criteria for progression. The recorded response is {reported}. Please review the response assessment.
messages.tips: This is the most consequential single error class in tumor data: it delays or entirely misses the progression date and directly biases progression-free survival. Always check the nadir visit shown above is itself a complete assessment.

rule.title: Complete response reported while measurable disease persists
rule.intent: Enforce the full complete response definition, including nodal short axis.
rule.logic: if reported_target_response == CR and ( any non-nodal target with state != ABSENT or any nodal target with short axis >= config.pathological_node_threshold_mm or any target with state in (TOO_SMALL_TO_MEASURE, NOT_EVALUABLE)): raise finding

messages.reviewPoint: Conditions required for a complete response of target lesions.
messages.issue: Subject {subject_id}, {visit}: complete response is reported for target lesions, but {blocking_description} (lesion {lesion_id}: {value} mm, state {state}).
messages.reason: A complete response of target lesions requires the disappearance of all non-nodal target lesions and a reduction of every pathological lymph node, whether target or non-target, to a short axis below {node_threshold} mm. A lesion that is still visible, including one recorded as too small to measure, is not a disappearance.
messages.query: A complete response is recorded at {visit}, but {blocking_description}. Please review the response assessment and the individual lesion records.
messages.tips: Note the asymmetry that causes most of these: the sum of diameters can be very small without a complete response being appropriate, because nodes retain a short axis. Conversely, complete response does not require the sum to be zero.

rule.title: Reported non-target response does not match the derived response
rule.intent: Recompute the non-target response and compare.
rule.logic: derived = nonTargetResponse(...) if reported_non_target_response != derived: raise finding

messages.reviewPoint: Derivation of the non-target lesion response from the individual non-target lesion states.
messages.issue: Subject {subject_id}, {visit}: non-target response is reported as {reported} but derives as {derived}. Lesion states: {non_target_breakdown}.
messages.reason: {derivation_explanation}
messages.query: The non-target lesion response recorded at {visit} is {reported}, while the individual non-target lesion assessments ({non_target_breakdown}) correspond to {derived}. Please review.
messages.tips: A complete response of non-target disease additionally requires every pathological lymph node to be below 10 mm short axis, and where the protocol uses tumor markers, normalisation of those markers.

rule.title: Non-target complete response reported while a pathological node persists
rule.intent: Nodal condition for non-target complete response.
rule.logic: if reported_non_target_response == CR and any non-target node with short axis >= config.pathological_node_threshold_mm: raise finding

messages.reviewPoint: Nodal condition for a complete response of non-target disease.
messages.issue: Subject {subject_id}, {visit}: non-target complete response is reported while node {lesion_id} ({organ}) measures {value} mm short axis.
messages.reason: A complete response requires all lymph nodes, target and non-target alike, to have reduced to a short axis below {node_threshold} mm. A node of {value} mm remains pathological, so the non-target response is Non-CR/Non-PD.
messages.query: A complete response of non-target lesions is recorded at {visit}, but node {lesion_id} measures {value} mm in short axis. Please review the non-target response.
messages.tips: Non-target nodes are often not measured at all; where the eCRF does not capture a short axis for non-target nodes, this check depends on the radiology narrative and may need to be raised as a clarification rather than a correction.

rule.title: Unequivocal non-target progression reported in a subject with responding or stable measurable disease
rule.intent: Apply the guideline's "exceptional circumstance" test.
rule.logic: if non_target_response == PD and target_response in (CR, PR, SD) and new_lesion != YES: raise finding LLM assesses the recorded non-target descriptions for evidence of substantial overall worsening; strong evidence downgrades to INFO

messages.reviewPoint: Threshold for declaring unequivocal progression of non-target disease when measurable disease is present.
messages.issue: Subject {subject_id}, {visit}: unequivocal progression of non-target disease is reported while the target lesion response is {target_response} (sum {sum} mm, {pct_nadir}% from nadir) and no new lesion is recorded. Non-target findings: {non_target_breakdown}.
messages.reason: RECIST states that where measurable disease is present, unequivocal progression based on non-target disease alone should be an exceptional circumstance: the increase in overall tumor burden must be comparable in magnitude to the increase that would be required to declare progression for measurable disease. A modest increase in one non-target lesion is not sufficient, particularly while the target lesions are {target_response}.
messages.query: Unequivocal progression of non-target disease is recorded at {visit} while the target lesions show {target_response}. Please confirm that the overall tumor burden has increased substantially, and provide the radiological description supporting unequivocal progression.
messages.tips: Genuine cases exist — for example a marked increase in a pleural effusion or in lymphangitic disease. The question to the site is not "is this wrong" but "what supports unequivocal". Where the answer supports it, accept and record the rationale so the same finding is not re-raised.

rule.title: Reported overall response does not match the RECIST overall response table
rule.intent: The overall response must follow from its three components.
rule.logic: derived = overallTimepointResponse(reported_target, reported_non_target, reported_new, has_measurable) if reported_overall != derived: raise finding note: computed from the REPORTED components, so this rule isolates table-application errors from measurement errors, which are covered by TE-RS-001 and TE-RS-005

messages.reviewPoint: Application of the RECIST overall response table to the reported target, non-target and new lesion components.
messages.issue: Subject {subject_id}, {visit}: overall response is reported as {reported_overall}, while the recorded components (target {target}, non-target {non_target}, new lesion {new_lesion}) correspond to {derived_overall}.
messages.reason: {table_explanation}
messages.query: The overall response recorded at {visit} is {reported_overall}. Based on the recorded components — target lesion response {target}, non-target response {non_target}, new lesions {new_lesion} — the overall response should be {derived_overall}. Please review.
messages.tips: The combinations most often mis-applied are: target complete response with persisting non-target disease, which is a partial response rather than a complete response; and any new lesion, which is progression regardless of the target and non-target results.

tests.test: target CR, non-target Non-CR/Non-PD, no new → PR
target PR, non-target CR, new lesion YES → PD
target NE, non-target Non-CR/Non-PD, no new → NE

rule.title: New lesion flag inconsistent with recorded new lesions
rule.intent: Cross-check the flag against the lesion records.
rule.logic: if new_lesion_flag == YES and no lesion with category NEW at this assessment: raise finding if new_lesion_flag == NO and a lesion with category NEW is first recorded here: raise finding

messages.reviewPoint: Consistency between the new lesion indicator and the recorded new lesion identifications.
messages.issue: Subject {subject_id}, {visit}: the new lesion indicator is {flag} while {lesion_situation}.
messages.reason: A new lesion is sufficient for progression on its own. If the indicator and the lesion records disagree, either progression has been declared without a documented lesion, or a documented new lesion has not been reflected in the response — both change the progression date.
messages.query: The new lesion indicator at {visit} is recorded as {flag} while {lesion_situation}. Please reconcile the new lesion records with the response assessment.
messages.tips: Check whether the lesion was recorded as a new lesion at a later visit than the one where it was first seen; the progression date follows the first observation.

rule.title: New lesion recorded but overall response is not progression
rule.intent: A confirmed new lesion always means progression under RECIST 1.1.
rule.logic: if new_lesion_flag == YES and reported_overall != PD: raise finding (under iRECIST the expected value is iUPD; see TE-IR-001)

messages.reviewPoint: Effect of an unequivocal new lesion on the overall timepoint response.
messages.issue: Subject {subject_id}, {visit}: an unequivocal new lesion is recorded ({new_lesion_description}) but the overall response is reported as {reported_overall}.
messages.reason: Under RECIST 1.1 the appearance of any unequivocal new lesion is progression, irrespective of the target and non-target responses. {irecist_note}
messages.query: A new lesion is recorded at {visit} while the overall response is {reported_overall}. Please confirm the new lesion and review the overall response assessment.
messages.tips: Where the finding is equivocal rather than unequivocal, the correct handling is to record it as equivocal and continue treatment, treating the timepoint as not evaluable and re-assessing at the next visit; if later confirmed, progression is dated to this visit.

rule.title: New lesion in an anatomical region not imaged at baseline
rule.intent: Ensure the region-not-imaged case was considered explicitly.
rule.requiredFields: imaging_metadata.regions_imaged (or inferred from baseline lesion organs and modality)
rule.logic: if new lesion organ/region was not covered by the baseline imaging: raise finding

messages.reviewPoint: Interpretation of a lesion found in a region that was not imaged at baseline.
messages.issue: Subject {subject_id}, {visit}: a new lesion is recorded in {organ}, a region that does not appear to have been imaged at baseline ({baseline_regions}).
messages.reason: A lesion identified in a region that was not scanned at baseline is considered a new lesion, and therefore progression, because pre-existing disease at that site cannot be excluded. The point of this check is to confirm that the site made this determination deliberately rather than by default, since the alternative interpretation — that the lesion was present but unimaged — is not permitted.
messages.query: A new lesion is recorded in {organ} at {visit}. Baseline imaging does not appear to have covered this region. Please confirm the finding represents a new lesion and that baseline imaging of this region was not performed.
messages.tips: Brain metastases are the usual case: many protocols do not require baseline brain imaging, so a first brain scan performed for symptoms yields lesions that must be treated as new. Confirm the protocol's imaging requirements before raising.

rule.title: New lesion based on FDG-PET without confirmatory anatomical imaging
rule.intent: Apply the PET rules for new lesion determination.
rule.logic: if new lesion method == PET and no corresponding CT/MRI finding at the same site and no negative baseline PET recorded: raise finding

messages.reviewPoint: Use of FDG-PET to establish a new lesion.
messages.issue: Subject {subject_id}, {visit}: a new lesion in {organ} is based on FDG-PET, without a corresponding finding on anatomical imaging and without a negative baseline PET.
messages.reason: A positive FDG-PET finding establishes a new lesion when the baseline PET was negative, or when the new site is confirmed on CT or MRI. Without either, a positive PET alone is not sufficient, because the finding may represent disease present but not FDG-avid or not imaged at baseline, or may be non-malignant uptake.
messages.query: The new lesion recorded at {visit} in {organ} is based on FDG-PET. Please confirm whether a baseline PET was performed and negative, or whether the lesion is confirmed on CT or MRI.
messages.tips: Inflammatory and infectious uptake is common, particularly under immunotherapy; anatomical confirmation matters most in that setting.

rule.title: Equivocal new lesion later confirmed but progression not back-dated
rule.intent: Progression is dated to the first observation of a lesion later confirmed.
rule.logic: if a lesion was EQUIVOCAL at visit i and confirmed unequivocal at visit j > i and the recorded progression date != date of visit i: raise finding

messages.reviewPoint: Dating of progression when an equivocal finding is subsequently confirmed.
messages.issue: Subject {subject_id}: lesion {lesion_id} was recorded as equivocal at {first_visit} ({first_date}) and confirmed at {confirm_visit} ({confirm_date}); the progression date is recorded as {recorded_pd_date}.
messages.reason: Where therapy continues after an equivocal finding and the finding is subsequently confirmed as a new lesion, progression is dated to the time of the initial observation, not to the confirming assessment. Using the later date overstates progression-free survival by {days_difference} days.
messages.query: Lesion {lesion_id} was equivocal at {first_visit} and confirmed at {confirm_visit}. Please confirm the date of progression; per RECIST the progression date should be the date of the initial observation ({first_date}).
messages.tips: Under iRECIST the handling differs — the iUPD and iCPD dates are both retained and the analysis convention is protocol-specific. Check which criteria govern before applying this rule.

rule.title: Complete or partial response counted as best overall response without confirmation
rule.intent: Enforce the protocol's confirmation requirement.
rule.logic: if config.response_confirmation_required and reported_best_overall_response in (CR, PR) and no subsequent assessment >= config.confirmation_min_interval_days later with a response of at least the same rank: raise finding

messages.reviewPoint: Confirmation of complete and partial responses where the protocol requires it.
