messages.issue: Subject {subject_id}: best overall response is recorded as {reported_bor} based on {first_visit} ({first_date}), but the next assessment {next_description} does not confirm it.
messages.reason: The protocol requires confirmation of a complete or partial response by a repeat assessment performed no less than {confirm_days} days after the criteria were first met. Without confirmation the response is unconfirmed and the derived best overall response is {derived_bor}. Counting unconfirmed responses inflates the objective response rate.
messages.query: The best overall response is recorded as {reported_bor} based on the assessment at {first_visit}. A confirmatory assessment at least {confirm_days} days later does not appear to support this response. Please review the best overall response.
messages.tips: Check whether a confirmatory scan exists but was entered as an unscheduled visit; also check the interval, since a confirmation performed too early does not satisfy the requirement.

rule.title: Reported best overall response does not match the derived best overall response
rule.intent: Recompute best overall response across the whole subject timeline.
rule.logic: derived = bestOverallResponse(orderedTimepoints, config) if reported_bor != derived.bor: raise finding

messages.reviewPoint: Derivation of best overall response across all timepoints, applying the confirmation requirement and excluding assessments after progression.
messages.issue: Subject {subject_id}: best overall response is reported as {reported_bor}; derived as {derived_bor}. Timepoint responses considered: {timepoint_sequence}.
messages.reason: {bor_explanation}
messages.query: The best overall response recorded for this subject is {reported_bor}. Based on the recorded timepoint responses ({timepoint_sequence}) and the protocol's confirmation requirement, the best overall response derives as {derived_bor}. Please review.
messages.tips: Two frequent causes: a response recorded after progression being counted, and a stable disease result assigned before the protocol's minimum duration from baseline has elapsed.

rule.title: Partial response or stable disease assigned to a subject without measurable disease at baseline
rule.intent: Non-target-only subjects have a restricted response vocabulary.
rule.logic: if subject has no target lesions at baseline and reported_overall in (PR, SD): raise finding

messages.reviewPoint: Permitted response categories for subjects with non-measurable disease only.
messages.issue: Subject {subject_id}, {visit}: overall response is reported as {reported_overall}, but no target lesions were selected at baseline.
messages.reason: A subject with non-measurable disease only can be assigned a complete response, Non-CR/Non-PD, progressive disease or not evaluable. Partial response and stable disease require measurable disease, since both are defined by a change in the sum of diameters. The corresponding category here is Non-CR/Non-PD.
messages.query: The overall response at {visit} is recorded as {reported_overall} although no target lesions were identified at baseline. Please review; for subjects with non-measurable disease only, the appropriate categories are complete response, Non-CR/Non-PD, progressive disease or not evaluable.
messages.tips: Check first whether target lesions were in fact selected but failed to load — a missing target lesion record produces this finding spuriously. Look for a companion structural finding on this subject.

rule.title: Stable disease assigned before the protocol's minimum duration
rule.intent: Stable disease requires a minimum interval from baseline.
rule.logic: if reported_overall == SD and (assessment_date - baseline_date) < config.sd_min_duration_days: raise finding

messages.reviewPoint: Minimum duration from baseline required before stable disease can be assigned.
messages.issue: Subject {subject_id}, {visit}: stable disease is reported {days} days after baseline; the protocol requires a minimum of {min_days} days.
messages.reason: Stable disease is meaningful only if maintained for a minimum interval defined by the protocol. An earlier assessment cannot establish stability, and counting it inflates the disease control rate.
messages.query: Stable disease is recorded at {visit}, {days} days after baseline, which is shorter than the minimum of {min_days} days specified in the protocol. Please review the response assessment.
messages.tips: This affects best overall response rather than the timepoint response in many conventions; confirm the sponsor's derivation convention before querying the site.

rule.title: Response recorded after a documented progression
rule.intent: Post-progression assessments must not contribute to response endpoints.
rule.logic: if an assessment after the first PD carries a response in (CR, PR, SD) and it contributes to the reported best overall response: raise finding

messages.reviewPoint: Treatment of assessments performed after progression in response derivation.
messages.issue: Subject {subject_id}: progression is recorded at {pd_visit} ({pd_date}), and a response of {response} is recorded at {later_visit} ({later_date}).
messages.reason: Best overall response is determined from the assessments recorded from the start of treatment until progression. Assessments after progression are retained in the data but do not contribute to the response endpoints. Including one here changes the best overall response from {derived_bor} to {reported_bor}.
messages.query: A response of {response} is recorded at {later_visit}, after progression was recorded at {pd_visit}. Please confirm the progression date and the response assessments.
messages.tips: Where the subject continued treatment beyond progression, the later assessments are legitimate data; the issue is their use in derivation, not their existence. If iRECIST applies, progression may have been unconfirmed and the later assessments are then fully valid — check the applicable criteria.

rule.title: Recorded progression date does not match the earliest assessment meeting progression criteria
rule.intent: Progression dating.
rule.logic: derived_date = progressionDate(orderedTimepoints, config) if |reported_progression_date - derived_date| > 0 days: raise finding

messages.reviewPoint: Dating of disease progression relative to the assessments that meet progression criteria.
messages.issue: Subject {subject_id}: progression date recorded as {reported_date}; the earliest assessment meeting progression criteria is {derived_visit} on {derived_date} ({days_difference} days difference).
messages.reason: Progression-free survival is measured to the date of the first assessment demonstrating progression. A difference of {days_difference} days changes the event time for this subject and, aggregated across subjects, biases the survival estimate.
messages.query: The progression date is recorded as {reported_date}, while the earliest assessment meeting progression criteria is {derived_visit} on {derived_date}. Please confirm the date of progression.
messages.tips: Distinguish radiological progression from clinical progression: if progression was determined clinically, the date may legitimately precede any imaging, and the record should say so.

rule.title: Investigator and independent central review assessments discordant
rule.intent: Surface discordance where both streams exist.

messages.reviewPoint: Concordance between the investigator assessment and the independent central review.
messages.issue: Subject {subject_id}, {visit}: investigator response {inv_response}, central review response {bicr_response}. {date_note}
messages.reason: Discordance between the investigator and central review is expected at some rate, but discordance that crosses a progression boundary affects the primary endpoint where the central review is the basis of analysis, and may indicate a systematic difference in lesion selection or measurement at this site.
messages.query: Not applicable: this finding is for internal review and reconciliation and is not normally issued as a site query.
messages.tips: Review the lesion-level data from both readers side by side. Consistent directional discordance at one site is a monitoring signal; scattered discordance is normal reader variability. Where the sponsor keeps the two streams deliberately separated, this rule should be disabled in configuration.

rule.title: RECIST 1.1 progression not recorded as unconfirmed progression under iRECIST
rule.intent: First progression under iRECIST is iUPD, never iCPD.
rule.logic: if guideline includes iRECIST and RECIST 1.1 criteria for PD are met at this timepoint and no prior iUPD exists and reported irecist_response != iUPD: raise finding

messages.reviewPoint: Assignment of unconfirmed progression when RECIST 1.1 progression criteria are first met under iRECIST.
messages.issue: Subject {subject_id}, {visit}: RECIST 1.1 progression criteria are met ({pd_driver_description}) and the iRECIST response is recorded as {reported_irecist}, with no preceding unconfirmed progression.
messages.reason: Under iRECIST, the first timepoint at which RECIST 1.1 progression criteria are met is assigned unconfirmed progression (iUPD). Confirmed progression (iCPD) can only be assigned at a subsequent assessment that demonstrates further worsening. Recording confirmed progression at first occurrence removes the confirmation step that iRECIST exists to provide, and may lead to treatment being discontinued for pseudoprogression.
messages.query: RECIST 1.1 progression criteria are met at {visit} and the iRECIST response is recorded as {reported_irecist}. Under iRECIST the first occurrence of progression should be recorded as unconfirmed progression (iUPD), with confirmation at the next assessment. Please review.
messages.tips: The commonest cause is the site applying RECIST 1.1 habits to an iRECIST study. Where both RECIST 1.1 and iRECIST responses are collected, the RECIST 1.1 field correctly reads PD while the iRECIST field should read iUPD — the two are not in conflict.

rule.title: Confirmatory assessment after unconfirmed progression missing or outside the window
rule.intent: iUPD must be followed by a confirmatory assessment within the protocol window.

messages.reviewPoint: Timing of the confirmatory assessment following unconfirmed progression.
messages.issue: Subject {subject_id}: unconfirmed progression recorded at {iupd_visit} ({iupd_date}); {confirmation_situation}.
messages.reason: iRECIST requires the confirmatory assessment between {window_min} and {window_max} days after unconfirmed progression. Assessing too early risks confirming transient pseudoprogression as true progression; assessing too late leaves the subject on a potentially ineffective therapy and leaves the progression date ambiguous. Without a confirmatory assessment, progression remains unconfirmed and the subject's progression status for analysis is indeterminate.
messages.query: Unconfirmed progression was recorded at {iupd_visit} on {iupd_date}. {confirmation_situation}. Please confirm whether a confirmatory tumor assessment was performed and enter the data, or record the reason it was not performed.
messages.tips: Where the subject discontinued treatment at unconfirmed progression, no confirmation is expected and this finding should be rejected with that reason; check the disposition data before querying.

rule.title: Confirmed progression assigned without meeting the confirmation criteria
rule.intent: iCPD requires further worsening in the category that drove iUPD.
rule.logic: if reported_irecist == iCPD: verify per driver recorded at the preceding iUPD: TARGET -> sum >= iUPD.sum + config.icpd_target_increment_mm NON_TARGET -> further unequivocal worsening recorded NEW_LESION -> new lesion sum >= iUPD.new_lesion_sum + config.icpd_new_lesion_increment_mm or additional new lesions or a new driver now independently meets RECIST 1.1 progression criteria if none satisfied: raise finding

messages.reviewPoint: Criteria for confirming progression under iRECIST.
messages.issue: Subject {subject_id}, {visit}: confirmed progression is recorded. Unconfirmed progression was driven by {driver} at {iupd_visit}; at this assessment {confirmation_evidence}.
messages.reason: Confirmation of progression requires further worsening in the category that drove the unconfirmed progression: an increase of at least {target_increment} mm in the target lesion sum relative to the unconfirmed progression timepoint, further unequivocal worsening of non-target disease, an increase of at least {new_increment} mm in the sum of new measurable lesions, or the appearance of additional new lesions. A new category independently meeting RECIST 1.1 progression criteria also confirms. None of these is evident here, so the response should remain unconfirmed progression or reset according to the current burden.
messages.query: Confirmed progression is recorded at {visit}. The unconfirmed progression at {iupd_visit} was driven by {driver}, and the current assessment shows {confirmation_evidence}. Please review the confirmation of progression against the iRECIST criteria.
messages.tips: Note the reference point: confirmation compares against the unconfirmed progression timepoint, not against the nadir. This differs from RECIST 1.1 and is a frequent source of confusion.

rule.title: New lesion measurements added to the baseline target sum
rule.intent: iRECIST tracks new lesions separately.
rule.logic: if reported_sum at a timepoint equals derived baseline-target sum + new lesion measurements (within tolerance) rather than the baseline-target sum alone: raise finding

messages.reviewPoint: Separate recording of new lesion measurements from the baseline target lesion sum under iRECIST.
messages.issue: Subject {subject_id}, {visit}: the reported sum of {reported} mm matches the baseline target sum ({target_sum} mm) plus the new lesion measurements ({new_sum} mm) rather than the target sum alone.
messages.reason: Under iRECIST, new lesions are recorded and measured separately from the baseline target lesions, with their own sum of up to five new measurable lesions, two per organ. They are never added to the baseline target sum, because the baseline sum must remain comparable to baseline for response assessment, while the new lesion sum is used to judge confirmation of progression. Combining them corrupts both.
messages.query: The sum of diameters at {visit} appears to include the measurements of new lesions. Under iRECIST new lesions are recorded and summed separately from the baseline target lesions. Please review the sum of diameters and the new lesion records.
messages.tips: Confirm the eCRF design supports separate new lesion recording; where it does not, this is a study set-up issue affecting every iRECIST subject rather than a site error.

rule.title: Response reset after unconfirmed progression not applied correctly
rule.intent: When progression is not confirmed, the response returns to iCR/iPR/iSD against the original nadir.

messages.reviewPoint: Reassignment of response when progression is not confirmed at the next assessment.
messages.issue: Subject {subject_id}, {visit}: unconfirmed progression at {iupd_visit} was not confirmed, and the response is recorded as {reported_irecist}; the derived response is {derived_irecist} (sum {sum} mm against the nadir of {nadir_sum} mm at {nadir_visit}).
messages.reason: If confirmation criteria are not met, the subject's response resets to iCR, iPR or iSD according to the current tumor burden measured against the original nadir. The nadir is not reset by the unconfirmed progression, so a later increase can again produce unconfirmed progression. This is the mechanism by which iRECIST accommodates pseudoprogression.
messages.query: Unconfirmed progression was recorded at {iupd_visit} and was not confirmed at {visit}. The response at {visit} is recorded as {reported_irecist}; based on the current sum of {sum} mm against the nadir of {nadir_sum} mm the response derives as {derived_irecist}. Please review.
messages.tips: Multiple episodes of unconfirmed progression are permitted and are not an error. What is not permitted is treating the unconfirmed progression sum as the new reference.

rule.title: New measurable lesions exceed the iRECIST limits
rule.intent: At most five new measurable lesions, two per organ.
rule.logic: if count(new measurable lesions) > config.max_new_target_lesions_total or count per organ > config.max_new_target_lesions_per_organ: raise finding

messages.reviewPoint: Limits on the number of new measurable lesions recorded and measured under iRECIST.
messages.issue: Subject {subject_id}: {n} new measurable lesions are recorded ({per_organ_breakdown}); iRECIST permits up to {max_total} in total and {max_per_organ} per organ.
messages.reason: The new lesion sum is used to judge confirmation of progression, so it must be constructed consistently. Additional new lesions beyond the limits are recorded as new non-target lesions rather than measured.
messages.query: {n} new measurable lesions are recorded for this subject. iRECIST permits up to {max_total} new measurable lesions in total, and {max_per_organ} per organ, with any further new lesions recorded as non-target. Please review the new lesion records.
messages.tips: The appearance of numerous new lesions is itself strong evidence of true progression, so this finding is usually a recording issue rather than a clinical question.

rule.title: Assessments continue after confirmed progression without documented rationale
rule.intent: iCPD is terminal for response derivation.
rule.logic: if assessments exist after an iCPD timepoint and are assigned iRECIST responses other than iCPD: raise finding

messages.reviewPoint: Handling of assessments performed after confirmed progression.
messages.issue: Subject {subject_id}: confirmed progression recorded at {icpd_visit} ({icpd_date}); subsequent assessments at {later_visits} carry responses of {later_responses}.
messages.reason: Confirmed progression is the terminal response state. Later assessments may be collected for follow-up, but assigning a non-progression response after confirmed progression is inconsistent and risks the later response being carried into the best overall response derivation.
messages.query: Assessments after the confirmed progression at {icpd_visit} carry responses of {later_responses}. Please confirm the progression status and the response assessments recorded after it.
messages.tips: Check whether the earlier assessment was in fact unconfirmed rather than confirmed progression; a mislabelled iCPD is the more likely error.

rule.title: Treatment continued beyond unconfirmed progression without documented clinical stability
rule.intent: iRECIST permits continuation only for clinically stable subjects.
rule.requiredFields: cross_domain.exposure, cross_domain.performance_status or clinical stability assessment
rule.logic: if treatment continued after an iUPD and no record of the clinical stability assessment exists at that timepoint: raise finding

messages.reviewPoint: Documentation of clinical stability when treatment continues beyond unconfirmed progression.
messages.issue: Subject {subject_id}: treatment continued after unconfirmed progression at {iupd_visit}, with no recorded assessment of clinical stability.
messages.reason: iRECIST permits treatment beyond unconfirmed progression only where the subject is clinically stable: no decline in performance status, no worsening of symptoms attributable to disease, and no need for intensified management. The documentation supports both subject safety and the interpretation of the subsequent assessment.
messages.query: Treatment continued after unconfirmed progression at {iupd_visit}. Please confirm that the subject was assessed as clinically stable at that time and that this is documented.
messages.tips: This is a protocol compliance point as much as a data point; where the eCRF has no field for it, escalate to the monitoring team rather than issuing a data query.

rule.title: RECIST 1.1 and iRECIST responses collected in parallel are mutually inconsistent
rule.intent: Where both are collected, the iRECIST value must follow from the RECIST 1.1 value and the state history.
rule.logic: expected = irecistStateMachine(...) applied to the reported RECIST 1.1 responses if reported_irecist != expected: raise finding

messages.reviewPoint: Consistency between the parallel RECIST 1.1 and iRECIST response assessments.
messages.issue: Subject {subject_id}, {visit}: RECIST 1.1 response {r11_response}, iRECIST response {reported_irecist}; the iRECIST response derived from the RECIST 1.1 sequence is {expected_irecist}.
messages.reason: The iRECIST assessment is derived from the same underlying measurements as the RECIST 1.1 assessment, differing only in the treatment of progression and new lesions. Given the RECIST 1.1 result at this timepoint and the preceding response history, the iRECIST response should be {expected_irecist}.
messages.query: The RECIST 1.1 and iRECIST responses recorded at {visit} are {r11_response} and {reported_irecist}. Based on the response history the iRECIST response would be expected to be {expected_irecist}. Please review.
messages.tips: Where the two fields are on separate forms completed by different people, expect systematic divergence at a site; treat that as a training signal rather than a per-record query.

rule.title: Study uses immunotherapy but responses are assessed under RECIST 1.1 only
rule.intent: Detect a study-level configuration mismatch.
rule.logic: if protocol specifies iRECIST and no iRECIST responses are present in the data, or the reverse: raise study-level finding

messages.reviewPoint: Alignment between the response criteria specified in the protocol and the response data collected.
messages.issue: Study {study_id}: the protocol specifies {configured_guideline}, but {observed_situation}.
messages.reason: If iRECIST is specified but not collected, pseudoprogression cannot be distinguished from true progression, and subjects may be discontinued prematurely. If iRECIST is collected but not specified, the analysis convention is undefined. Either way the endpoint derivation is at risk across the whole study.
messages.query: Not applicable: this is a study set-up finding for the study team rather than a site query.
messages.tips: Raise with the study data manager and the biostatistician; resolution usually requires a database change rather than data correction.

rule.title: End of treatment due to progression but no progression recorded in the tumor data
rule.logic: if disposition reason indicates progressive disease and no assessment with overall response PD (or iCPD) exists: raise finding

messages.reviewPoint: Consistency between the reason for treatment discontinuation and the recorded tumor response.
messages.issue: Subject {subject_id}: treatment discontinued on {disposition_date} for {disposition_reason}, but no assessment records progressive disease. Last recorded response: {last_response} at {last_visit}.
messages.reason: If treatment stopped for progression, either an assessment demonstrating progression is missing from the tumor data, or the discontinuation reason is incorrect. Both affect the progression-free survival analysis: a missing progression event leads to censoring instead of an event.
messages.query: Treatment was discontinued for {disposition_reason} on {disposition_date}, but no tumor assessment recording progression is present. Please confirm whether a tumor assessment demonstrating progression was performed, and enter the data if so; if progression was determined clinically, please confirm the basis and the date.
messages.tips: Clinical progression without radiological confirmation is legitimate and common near end of life; the record should show it as such rather than leaving the tumor data silent.

rule.title: Progression recorded in the tumor data but treatment continued without documented rationale

messages.reviewPoint: Continuation of study treatment after documented progression.
messages.issue: Subject {subject_id}: progression recorded at {pd_visit} ({pd_date}); study treatment continued until {last_dose_date}, {days} days beyond progression.
messages.reason: Treatment beyond progression may be permitted by the protocol, but it must be documented, and it changes the interpretation of subsequent assessments. Where it is not permitted, this is a protocol deviation. Where the study uses iRECIST, the earlier assessment may have been unconfirmed progression rather than confirmed progression, in which case continuation is expected and the response coding needs review instead.
messages.query: Study treatment continued for {days} days after the progression recorded at {pd_visit}. Please confirm the progression assessment and whether continuation beyond progression was approved.
messages.tips: Check the applicable response criteria first — under iRECIST this pattern is normal and the finding should be rejected.

rule.title: New anticancer therapy started before recorded progression
rule.logic: if a new systemic anticancer therapy starts before the recorded progression date (or before any recorded progression): raise finding

messages.reviewPoint: Timing of new anticancer therapy relative to the recorded progression.
messages.issue: Subject {subject_id}: new anticancer therapy ({therapy}) started on {therapy_date}; recorded progression date {pd_date_or_none}.
messages.reason: Starting a new anticancer therapy before recorded progression usually indicates that progression occurred but was not captured, or that treatment changed for another documented reason. In progression-free survival analyses the start of new therapy is commonly a censoring or event-defining event, so the discrepancy has direct analytical consequences, and any tumor assessment after the new therapy no longer reflects the study treatment.
messages.query: A new anticancer therapy ({therapy}) started on {therapy_date}, before any recorded disease progression. Please confirm the reason for starting new therapy and whether a tumor assessment demonstrating progression was performed.
messages.tips: Radiotherapy for symptom palliation is a frequent benign explanation; distinguish it from a change of systemic therapy.

rule.title: Local therapy applied to a target lesion during the study
rule.logic: if radiotherapy, surgery or ablation is recorded at a site matching a target lesion after baseline: raise finding on all subsequent assessments of that lesion

messages.reviewPoint: Effect of locoregional therapy on the interpretation of a target lesion.
messages.issue: Subject {subject_id}: {procedure} was applied to {site} on {procedure_date}, matching target lesion {lesion_id}; measurements of this lesion continue at {later_visits}.
messages.reason: Once a lesion has received locoregional therapy, its subsequent size no longer reflects the systemic treatment effect, and RECIST treats such lesions as non-measurable unless progression is demonstrated. Continuing to include it in the sum understates tumor burden and can produce a spurious partial response.
messages.query: {procedure} was applied to {site} on {procedure_date}, which corresponds to target lesion {lesion_id}. Please confirm and clarify how this lesion has been assessed at subsequent visits.
messages.tips: The usual analytical convention is that the subject is considered to have progressed, or is censored, at the time of local therapy to a target lesion; confirm the protocol's convention with the statistician.

rule.title: Adverse event indicating disease progression without a corresponding tumor assessment
rule.logic: if an AE term maps to disease progression / malignant neoplasm progression and no PD assessment exists within config.ae_pd_window_days (default 60): raise finding

messages.reviewPoint: Consistency between adverse events indicating disease progression and the tumor assessment data.
messages.issue: Subject {subject_id}: adverse event "{ae_term}" with onset {ae_date}; no tumor assessment recording progression within {window} days.
messages.reason: An adverse event of disease progression implies a clinical determination of progression. If the tumor data does not reflect it, the progression event may be missing from the efficacy analysis, or the adverse event may have been coded inappropriately — disease progression is frequently reported as an adverse event when it should be captured as an efficacy outcome.
messages.query: An adverse event of "{ae_term}" is recorded with onset {ae_date}. Please confirm whether disease progression was documented and whether a tumor assessment was performed at that time.
messages.tips: Many sponsors instruct sites not to report disease progression as an adverse event; where that convention applies, the finding is also a coding issue for the safety team.

rule.title: Death recorded before the last tumor assessment or before the progression date
rule.logic: if death_date < last assessment_date or death_date < recorded progression date: raise finding

messages.reviewPoint: Consistency of the death date with the tumor assessment and progression dates.
messages.issue: Subject {subject_id}: death recorded on {death_date}; {conflicting_record} dated {conflict_date}.
messages.reason: A tumor assessment or progression date after the date of death is impossible, so one of the dates is wrong. Both feed survival and progression-free survival analyses directly.
messages.query: The date of death ({death_date}) precedes {conflicting_record} ({conflict_date}). Please verify both dates.
messages.tips: Partial dates are a frequent cause; check whether an imputed date is being compared against a complete one.

rule.title: Tumor marker not normalised while a complete response is reported
rule.logic: if reported overall response == CR and marker value > upper limit of normal: raise finding

messages.reviewPoint: Normalisation of tumor markers as a condition of complete response, where the protocol requires it.
messages.issue: Subject {subject_id}, {visit}: complete response reported while {marker} is {value} {unit} (upper limit of normal {uln}).
messages.reason: Where the protocol includes tumor markers in the response definition, a complete response requires marker normalisation in addition to the disappearance of all lesions. A persistently elevated marker means the response is Non-CR/Non-PD.
messages.query: A complete response is recorded at {visit} while {marker} remains above the upper limit of normal ({value} {unit}). Please review the response assessment.
messages.tips: Marker elevation can have non-malignant causes; the site's explanation may be sufficient without a data change.

rule.title: Imaging modality not among those permitted by the protocol
rule.logic: if measurement method not in config.allowed_modalities: raise finding

messages.reviewPoint: Use of imaging modalities permitted by the protocol and imaging charter.
messages.issue: Subject {subject_id}, {visit}: lesion {lesion_id} assessed by {method}; the protocol permits {allowed_modalities}.
messages.reason: Modalities differ in sensitivity and in measurement reproducibility. Using a modality outside the protocol makes the measurement non-comparable with the rest of the subject's data and with other subjects.
messages.query: Lesion {lesion_id} was assessed by {method} at {visit}, which is not among the modalities specified in the protocol. Please confirm the modality used.
messages.tips: Contrast versus non-contrast CT is the most consequential variant and is often not captured as a distinct modality; consider whether the eCRF should distinguish them.

rule.title: Required disease-site imaging missing
rule.logic: if the protocol requires imaging of a region (e.g. brain in a study enrolling subjects with brain metastases) and no assessment covers that region: raise finding

messages.reviewPoint: Coverage of all protocol-required anatomical regions at each assessment.
messages.issue: Subject {subject_id}, {visit}: no assessment of {required_region} although the protocol requires it{subject_context}.
messages.reason: Disease in an unimaged region cannot be assessed, and a lesion later found there must be treated as a new lesion. Missing required imaging therefore both reduces the reliability of the current response and risks a spurious progression later.
messages.query: No assessment of {required_region} is recorded at {visit} although the protocol requires it. Please confirm whether the imaging was performed and enter the results.
messages.tips: Brain imaging is the usual case, particularly in lung cancer and melanoma studies.

rule.title: Best overall response inconsistent with the subject's timepoint responses at study level
rule.logic: if reported_bor rank is better than the best reported timepoint response: raise finding

messages.reviewPoint: Consistency of the recorded best overall response with the recorded timepoint responses.
messages.issue: Subject {subject_id}: best overall response recorded as {reported_bor}, while the best timepoint response recorded is {best_timepoint} at {visit}.
messages.reason: The best overall response cannot be better than any response actually recorded at a timepoint. This indicates either a missing timepoint assessment or an incorrect best overall response.
messages.query: The best overall response is recorded as {reported_bor}, but the best response recorded at any timepoint is {best_timepoint}. Please review.
messages.tips: Check for an unscheduled assessment that was not entered; a response confirmed at an unscheduled visit is a common cause.

rule.title: Subject has no post-baseline assessment
rule.logic: if subject has a baseline assessment, received treatment, and has no post-baseline tumor assessment: raise finding

messages.reviewPoint: Availability of at least one post-baseline tumor assessment for each treated subject.
messages.issue: Subject {subject_id}: treated from {first_dose_date} with no post-baseline tumor assessment; last known status {status}.
messages.reason: A treated subject with no post-baseline assessment is not evaluable for response and is censored at randomisation or treatment start in progression-free survival, which reduces the power of the analysis. The reason should be documented.
messages.query: No post-baseline tumor assessment is recorded for this subject. Please confirm whether an assessment was performed, and record the reason if it was not.
messages.tips: Early death or early withdrawal are the usual explanations and are legitimate; the finding exists to ensure the reason is captured.

rule.title: Site-level pattern of the same finding
rule.logic: if a rule fires for >= config.site_pattern_min_subjects (default 3) subjects at one site and the site's rate exceeds the study rate by config.site_pattern_factor (default 3): raise one aggregate finding and link the individual findings

messages.reviewPoint: Detection of systematic issues at a site rather than isolated data errors.
messages.issue: Site {site_id}: rule {source_rule_id} ({source_rule_title}) fires for {n_subjects} of {site_subjects} subjects, against a study rate of {study_rate}%.
messages.reason: A concentration of the same issue at one site usually reflects a training or process gap rather than isolated errors. Addressing it at the site level resolves the whole cluster and prevents recurrence, whereas issuing individual queries treats the symptom.
messages.query: Not applicable: this finding is directed to the monitoring team rather than to the site as a data query.
messages.tips: Pair with a site training action and re-check at the next data cut; the recurrence status on the linked findings will show whether the intervention worked.

rule.title: Finding already covered by an open query
rule.logic: classification produced by the query reconciler; see queryReconciliation

messages.reviewPoint: Suppression of findings already covered by an outstanding query.
messages.issue: Subject {subject_id}, {visit}: finding {source_finding_id} is already covered by open query {query_id} raised on {opened_date}.
messages.reason: Re-issuing a query that is already outstanding creates duplicate work at the site and confuses the audit trail. The finding is retained and linked, but is suppressed from the default worklist until the query is answered.
messages.query: Not applicable: no new query is required.
messages.tips: If the outstanding query is materially different in scope from this finding, disposition the finding as NEW manually and issue a distinct query.

rule.title: Query answered or closed but the underlying issue persists
rule.logic: if a query matching this finding has status ANSWERED or CLOSED and the finding still evaluates as true against the current data: escalate severity by one level

messages.reviewPoint: Verification that answered and closed queries actually resolved the underlying data issue.
messages.issue: Subject {subject_id}, {visit}: query {query_id} was {query_status} on {resolution_date} with the answer "{answer_summary}", but the data still shows {current_state}.
messages.reason: The query was resolved without the data being corrected, or the correction did not address the issue. This is a higher-risk state than a new finding, because the issue has already been reviewed once and has passed through the query process unresolved.
messages.query: Query {query_id} regarding {issue_summary} was answered on {resolution_date}, but the data still shows {current_state}. Please clarify: if the data is correct as entered, please explain the basis; otherwise please make the correction.
messages.tips: Read the original answer before re-querying. Where the site confirmed the data is correct, the right next step is often a discussion with the medical monitor rather than a repeated query.

rule.title: Issue recurs after a previous resolution
rule.logic: if a finding with this dedupe key was RESOLVED in an earlier run and evaluates true again in the current run: mark RECURRENT and escalate

messages.reviewPoint: Recurrence of a previously resolved issue.
messages.issue: Subject {subject_id}, {visit}: this issue was resolved on {previous_resolution_date} (run {previous_run_id}) and is present again in the current data.
messages.reason: A recurrence usually means either that a data correction was reverted, or that a subsequent data entry reintroduced the same error. Both are worth understanding, because the same cause is likely to affect other records.
messages.query: This issue was previously raised and resolved on {previous_resolution_date}, and is present again in the current data. Please confirm the current value and clarify the reason for the change.
messages.tips: Compare the audit trail of the affected field across the two data cuts; a reverted correction and a fresh error need different responses.

rule.title: Critical query outstanding beyond the ageing threshold
rule.logic: if a query linked to a CRITICAL finding is OPEN for > config.query_aging_days (default 30): raise finding

messages.reviewPoint: Ageing of outstanding queries linked to endpoint-critical findings.
messages.issue: Subject {subject_id}: query {query_id} concerning {issue_summary} has been open for {days} days.
messages.reason: Endpoint-critical data cannot be locked while the query is outstanding, and late resolution compresses the timeline before database lock. Ageing queries on response data are a leading cause of lock delay.
messages.query: Not applicable: this finding is for the study team's query management rather than a new site query.
messages.tips: Escalate through the monitoring team rather than by reissuing the query.

rule.title: Query answer does not address the question asked
rule.logic: LLM classifies the answer against the query as {addresses: full | partial | none, intent: data_will_be_corrected | data_confirmed_correct | clarification_provided | unrelated, confidence} raise when addresses == none or partial with confidence >= 0.7

messages.reviewPoint: Responsiveness of query answers to the question asked.
messages.issue: Subject {subject_id}: query {query_id} asked "{query_summary}"; the answer "{answer_summary}" appears to {addresses_description}.
messages.reason: An unresponsive answer that is nonetheless accepted closes the query without resolving the underlying data question, so the issue survives into the locked database.
messages.query: Thank you for the response to query {query_id}. The original question concerned {query_summary}; could you please also confirm {outstanding_point}?
messages.tips: Site answers are often correct but terse. Read the original answer in full before re-querying; the model flags candidates rather than making the determination.

rule.title: Data changed after a query but a new inconsistency was introduced
rule.logic: if a data value changed between runs in response to a query and a NEW finding with a different rule id now exists on the same record: link and raise

messages.reviewPoint: Verification that data corrections did not introduce new inconsistencies.
messages.issue: Subject {subject_id}, {visit}: {field} was changed from {old_value} to {new_value} following query {query_id}; the record now triggers {new_rule_id} ({new_rule_title}).
messages.reason: Corrections made in isolation frequently break a dependent value — most often a lesion measurement corrected without the sum or the response being updated. The correction should be applied consistently across the dependent fields.
messages.query: Following the correction to {field} at {visit}, {new_issue_summary}. Please review the related fields so the assessment is internally consistent.
messages.tips: This is why measurement corrections should always be reviewed together with the sum and the response for the same timepoint, and for all later timepoints if the nadir moved.

llmIntegration.capabilityNegotiation:
strategy = select_strategy(adapter.capabilities, task.requirements) if adapter supports CONSTRAINED_JSON_SCHEMA -> constrained decoding, single call elif adapter supports JSON_MODE -> JSON mode + schema validation else -> prompt-enforced JSON + schema validation
on validation failure: attempt 1 repair call: original prompt + the validation error + "return only valid JSON" on second failure: record validation_status=FAILED, fall back to the deterministic template, and log the event; the finding is still produced, with template text.

prompt.inputs: lesion organ, laterality, location text, description text, method, guideline extract
prompt.outputSchema: {is_non_measurable: boolean, category: string|null, confidence: number, rationale: string}
prompt.constraint: Rationale must quote the input text it relies on. No output field may contain a measurement value.

prompt.inputs: non-target lesion descriptions at this and the previous timepoint, target response, sum change, guideline extract on unequivocal progression
prompt.outputSchema: {supports_unequivocal: boolean, magnitude_comment: string, confidence: number, rationale: string}

prompt.inputs: candidate finding summary; up to N historical queries for the same subject (text, status, dates)
evidence object, rule metadata, message templates, guideline citation, indication context
prompt.constraint: Every numeric value and identifier must appear as a placeholder token; the template engine substitutes them after generation and rejects the output if any placeholder is missing or any unexpected number appears.
Tone: factual, non-accusatory, addressed to a site coordinator; no clinical advice; no speculation about cause beyond what the evidence supports.

guardrails.guardrail: Numbers are never taken from model output. The template engine re-injects them from the evidence object and fails the render if the model removed a placeholder.

All site-authored text is wrapped in a labelled data envelope with an explicit instruction that its content is data only. Post-generation, any output containing instruction-like content that did not originate in the template is rejected and the template fallback is used. Site text that appears to contain instructions is itself surfaced as an INFO finding.
The adjudication response schema has no field capable of creating or deleting a finding; it can only set confidence, rationale, and (where downgradeable) a downgrade flag.
temperature=0 and a fixed seed where the provider supports it. Narrative variation across runs is expected and acceptable; verdict variation is not possible by construction.
Subject identifiers are pseudonymised and free text is scrubbed before any external call, per the study's egress policy. The mapping stays inside the trust boundary.
Evidence is deterministically summarised to fit the configured prompt budget (NFR-05). Truncation is explicit and recorded, never silent.

llmIntegration.conformanceSuite: A fixed fixture set runs against every configured adapter before it is approved for a study. Assertions: (1) deterministic verdicts identical across adapters; (2) schema validation success rate above the configured threshold; (3) narrative rubric score above threshold on a sample; (4) no placeholder loss; (5) injection fixtures do not alter behaviour. Results are stored with the adapter and model id and form part of the validation package.

queryReconciliation.matchingAlgorithm:
for each candidate finding f: # 1. exact match: queries TEA itself raised exact = queries where tea_rule_id == f.rule_id and subject == f.subject and assessment/lesion scope overlaps f # 2. structural match: same subject + visit + form/field or lesion structural = queries where subject == f.subject and (assessment matches or lesion matches) and field maps to one of f.evidence.fields # 3. semantic match (LLM, only over the residue) semantic = P-MATCH-QUERY(f.summary, remaining queries for this subject) filtered to relation == "same_issue" and confidence >= 0.75
matched = exact ∪ structural ∪ semantic if matched is empty: f.status = NEW elif any matched.status == OPEN: f.status = DUPLICATE_OPEN elif any matched.status in (ANSWERED, CLOSED): if f still evaluates true on current data: f.status = ANSWERED_UNRESOLVED # escalate else: f.status = ANSWERED_RESOLVED # not surfaced if f.dedupe_key was RESOLVED in a prior run and is true now: f.status = RECURRENT

safeguards.safeguard: Semantic matching may only suppress a finding of severity MINOR or INFO. For MAJOR and CRITICAL findings a semantic match links the query but leaves the finding visible, flagged "possible duplicate".
Suppression is never silent: suppressed findings are listed in a dedicated view with their linking query.
Escalation for ANSWERED_UNRESOLVED raises severity by one level, capped at CRITICAL, and records the original severity.

prioritisation.cascadeGrouping: Root-cause ordering within a subject: structural (ST) > baseline (BL) > measurement (FU) > response (RS/IR) > cross-domain (XD) If a finding of a higher-order family exists for the same subject and overlapping assessments, lower-order findings that are plausibly downstream are attached as `related_finding_ids` of the root and are collapsed under it in the worklist by default. They remain individually addressable. Example: TE-BL-001 (too many targets) collapses the TE-RS-001 mismatches it necessarily causes.
prioritisation.scoring: priority_score = severity_weight * endpoint_impact_weight # 1.5 if the finding changes a derived response, # progression date or best overall response; else 1.0 * query_state_weight # 1.3 ANSWERED_UNRESOLVED, 1.2 RECURRENT, # 0.3 DUPLICATE_OPEN, 1.0 NEW * confidence # 1.0 deterministic; model-reported for adjudicated * recency_weight # 1.1 if first seen in the current run severity_weight: CRITICAL 100, MAJOR 40, MINOR 10, INFO 2 The formula is displayed in the UI so a reviewer can see why an item ranks where it does.

outputSpecification.dedupeKey: dedupe_key = sha256(study_id | subject_id | rule_id | sorted(assessment_scope) | sorted(lesion_scope) | rule_semantic_version_major) Stable across runs and across PATCH/MINOR rule changes, so a finding's history survives rule wording updates. A MAJOR rule change deliberately produces a new key, because the issue being asserted has changed.
outputSpecification.coverageReport: Every run emits, alongside the findings: rules executed, rules deactivated with the reason and the missing fields, subjects and assessments evaluated, subjects partially evaluated with the reason, and counts by family and severity. A run with no findings is only meaningful alongside this report.

Formatted report per run or per subject, for the trial master file

errorHandling.policy: Structural defects become ST findings; the run continues with affected subjects marked partially evaluable.
A derivation that cannot complete for a subject marks that subject not evaluable with a reason; other subjects are unaffected.
An exception in one rule is caught, recorded as a run-level defect, and the remaining rules continue. A rule that fails is reported as NOT_EVALUATED in the coverage report, never as passing.
Timeouts, schema failures and outages fall back to deterministic behaviour and are logged; the run completes.
A write failure aborts the run; partial runs are never exposed.

performance.target: Deterministic full run: 500 subjects × 12 assessments in under 5 minutes (NFR-03).
performance.technique: Per-subject parallelism; rules are pure functions of a subject's data, so the workload partitions cleanly.
Narrative generation is deferred and batched: findings are persisted with template text immediately and enriched asynchronously, so the worklist is usable before narration completes.
Narrative caching keyed on (rule_id, rule_version, prompt_version, model_id, evidence hash) — identical evidence never re-generates.
Incremental runs process only subjects whose data changed since the previous snapshot (FR-16), with a full run at each data cut.

testing.level: Every function in , with boundary fixtures at every threshold: 30% PR, 20%/5 mm PD, 10 mm and 15 mm nodal, 5 mm iCPD increment, confirmation interval boundaries.
Each rule requires at least one positive and one negative fixture; CI fails if either is missing. Rules with false-positive guards require a fixture exercising the guard.
The published RECIST 1.1 and iRECIST worked examples are encoded as fixtures and must reproduce exactly.
A curated study with a signed-off expected finding list, run on every commit. Any difference must be acknowledged in the rule pack change history before merge.
The suite described in , run per adapter and per model version.
Fixtures containing instruction-like site text; assertion is that behaviour is unchanged and the text is flagged.
Synthetic study at the NFR-03 scale, run in CI on a schedule rather than per commit.
Reviewer tasks on a de-identified real study, against the Step 3 acceptance thresholds.

configuration.item: Per study, versioned and hashed; see the ProtocolConfig entity in the plan.
Per study: rules may be deactivated with a documented reason, which appears in the coverage report.
Tolerances (sum, percentage, dates), outlier bounds, ageing thresholds, site pattern thresholds.
Provider, model id, endpoint, budget, egress policy, redaction level, deterministic-only switch.
Query salutation, sign-off, and house phrasing conventions, applied by the template engine.
configuration.rule: No configuration value may be introduced as a literal in rule code. CI scans for numeric literals in rule modules.

procedure.name: Adding a review point
procedure.step: Add a rule entry to this catalog with a new permanent id, guideline basis, severity, logic, guards and the five message templates.
Implement the rule module with the same id; it must be a pure function of (canonical model, derived values, config).
Add at least one positive and one negative fixture, plus a guard fixture where guards exist.
Bump the rule pack MINOR version and record the addition in the change history.
Run the golden dataset; acknowledge any change in expected findings.

procedure.name: Adding a guideline or criteria set
procedure.step: Add a guideline profile with its parameter defaults.
Add derivation variants only where the algorithm genuinely differs; otherwise parameterise the existing ones.
Tag rules with the guideline versions they apply to.
Bump the rule pack MAJOR version if any existing rule's behaviour changes.

procedure.name: Adding a source system
procedure.step: Implement a new adapter producing the canonical input contract. No other layer changes.

procedure.name: Adding an LLM provider
procedure.step: Implement the adapter interface, declare its capability matrix, run the conformance suite, record the results in the validation package.

openSpecificationQuestions.question: Confirm the severity assigned to each rule against sponsor conventions; severities drive prioritisation and the lock criteria.
Confirm the interpretation decisions ID-01 to ID-08, in particular the too-small-to-measure convention and the treatment of reappearing lesions.
Confirm which PROPOSED_OPTIONAL rules (TE-BL-016, TE-IR-008) should be activated.
Confirm the query text style: salutation, level of explanation, whether the guideline reference should appear in the query itself or only in the reviewer-facing tips.
Confirm tolerances: sum tolerance in mm, percentage tolerance, date tolerances for BICR comparison.
Confirm whether findings addressed to the study team rather than the site (TE-RS-020, TE-IR-010, TE-XD-012, TE-QM-004) should be a separate finding class in the UI.
Confirm whether the sum of diameters is collected at all, or derived only — some eCRFs do not collect it, which makes TE-BL-011 and TE-FU-001 inapplicable and shifts weight onto TE-RS-001.
